Title: Uplift modeling and its implications for B2B customer churn prediction: A segmentation-based modeling approach
Authors: De Caigny A.; Coussement K.; Verbeke W.; Idbenjra K.; Phan M.
Abstract: Business-to-business (B2B) customer retention relies heavily on analytics and predictive modeling to support decision making. Given this, we introduce uplift modeling as a relevant prescriptive analytics tool. In particular, the uplift logit leaf model offers a segmentation-based algorithm that combines predictive performance with interpretability. Applied to a real-world data set of 6432 customers of a European software provider, the uplift logit leaf model achieves superior performance relative to three other popular uplift models in our study. The accessibility of output gained from the uplift logit leaf model also is showcased with a case study, which reveals relevant managerial insights. This new tool thus delivers novel insights in the form of customized, global, and segment-level visualizations that are especially pertinent to industrial marketing settings. Overall, the findings affirm the viability of uplift modeling for improving decisions related to B2B customer retention management. © 2021 Elsevier Inc.
Keywords: Churn prediction; Customer retention; Interpretability; Segmentation-based modeling; Uplift modeling; Visualization
keywords: customer retention, analytics, predictive modeling, uplift modeling, segmentation, managerial insights
rationale: The abstract discusses the application of uplift modeling and predictive analytics to improve B2B customer retention decisions. It emphasizes the importance of market analysis and segmentation-based algorithms, which aligns with the Thinking AI category focused on market analysis and targeting. The findings provide insights that can enhance decision-making processes, indicating a strategic analytical application rather than purely mechanical or emotional.
resumo: A retenção de clientes em negócios B2B depende fortemente de análises e modelagem preditiva para apoiar a tomada de decisões. Neste contexto, introduzimos a modelagem de uplift como uma ferramenta analítica prescritiva relevante. Em particular, o modelo de uplift logit leaf oferece um algoritmo baseado em segmentação que combina desempenho preditivo com interpretabilidade. Aplicado a um conjunto de dados real de 6432 clientes de um provedor de software europeu, o modelo de uplift logit leaf alcança desempenho superior em relação a outros três modelos populares de uplift estudados. A acessibilidade dos resultados obtidos com o modelo de uplift logit leaf também é demonstrada por meio de um estudo de caso, que revela insights gerenciais relevantes. Essa nova ferramenta, portanto, fornece insights inovadores na forma de visualizações personalizadas, globais e em nível de segmento, especialmente pertinentes a ambientes de marketing industrial. No geral, os resultados confirmam a viabilidade da modelagem de uplift para melhorar decisões relacionadas à gestão de retenção de clientes B2B.

Title: Analysis of purchase history data based on a new latent class model for RFM analysis
Authors: Zhang Q.; Yamashita H.; Mikawa K.; Goto M.
Abstract: Recently, it has become easier to make use of various kinds of information on customers (e.g. customers' purchase history), due to the development of information technology. Especially in the marketing field, in fact, many companies try to employ customer segmentation for the services customization which leads to increase customer loyalty and to keep high customer retention. One of the well-known approaches for the customer analysis based on purchase history data is the RFM analysis. The RFM analysis is usually used to segment customers into several groups by using three variables; how long it has been since their last purchase, how many times they purchased, and how much they spent. However, the conventional method of the RFM analysis did not assume a generative model. Therefore, when applying to an actual data set and scoring each index of R, F, M scores, several problems occur. The main problem is that an analyst should arbitrarily decide the threshold for the scores of RFM. On the other hand, in the field of machine learning, the probabilistic latent semantic analysis is widely used for soft clustering. The latent class model enables us to cluster customers into latent classes and to calculate the assignment probabilities of each customer to each latent class. In this paper, we propose a new latent class model for the RFM analysis based on the purchase history data. The proposed model enables to decide the scoring of RFM and segment customers automatically, and the soft clustering approach helps the interpretation of the result. Furthermore, the proposed model takes account of the generation model of RFM scores. From the result of actual data analysis, it became clear that it is possible to extract latent classes that express the statistical characteristics of data well. Given a generative model estimated from the given data, it is also possible to predict future purchase behaviors of customers or to generate virtual data for simulation analysis and make decisions based on the result. We verify the effectiveness of our model by analyzing a real purchase history data of a Japanese major retail company. © 2020 KIIE
Keywords: Latent Class Model; Marketing Segmentation; RFM Analysis
keywords: customer segmentation, RFM analysis, latent class model, purchase behavior, data analysis
rationale: The abstract discusses a new approach to customer segmentation using RFM analysis and a latent class model, which aligns with market analysis and strategic targeting in marketing. The focus on analyzing customer purchase behavior and predicting future actions falls under the scope of Thinking AI, which emphasizes market analysis and targeting. The abstract does not emphasize emotional understanding or mechanical processes, but rather highlights analytical models for customer behavior predictions.
resumo: Recentemente, o uso de informações sobre clientes, como o histórico de compras, tornou-se mais acessível devido ao avanço da tecnologia da informação. No campo do marketing, muitas empresas utilizam a segmentação de clientes para personalizar serviços, aumentando a lealdade e a retenção de clientes. A análise RFM, que segmenta clientes com base em três variáveis (tempo desde a última compra, frequência de compras e valor gasto), é uma abordagem conhecida, mas não assume um modelo gerador, o que pode levar a problemas na definição de limites para as pontuações. Em contraste, a análise semântica latente probabilística é utilizada em aprendizado de máquina para agrupamento suave. Este artigo propõe um novo modelo de classe latente para a análise RFM, que automatiza a segmentação de clientes e considera o modelo gerador das pontuações RFM. A análise de dados reais demonstrou que é possível extrair classes latentes que representam bem as características estatísticas dos dados, permitindo prever comportamentos de compra futuros e gerar dados virtuais para análises de simulação. A eficácia do modelo foi verificada com dados de uma grande empresa de varejo japonesa.

Title: Joint selection of variables and clusters: recovering the underlying structure of marketing data
Authors: Brudvig S.; Brusco M.J.; Cradit J.D.
Abstract: Clustering observations into groups is perhaps one of the more common marketing analytic techniques. Many variable-selection procedures are available for clustering, and some have exhibited good performance in simulation studies. Unfortunately, the best-performing methods often fail because they emphasize the clustering power of individual variables. For this reason, we recommend extreme caution when using the existing procedures, and we argue that enumeration of all-possible variable subsets is a preferred strategy. We also address a common decision problem—the selection of the number of clusters—and develop an index which can help guide the joint selection of variables and clusters. By way of an empirical example, we illustrate the variable-selection problem and demonstrate the use of the proposed index to jointly select variables and clusters in K-means partitioning. © 2018, Springer Nature Limited.
Keywords: K-means clustering; New product launch; Pharmaceutical industry; Segmentation; Variable selection
keywords: clustering, variable selection, market analysis, K-means partitioning, empirical example
rationale: The abstract discusses the clustering of observations and variable selection procedures, which falls under the category of market analysis. It emphasizes the importance of selecting the right variables and clusters, indicating a strategic approach typical of Thinking AI. Additionally, the development of an index for guiding variable and cluster selection further aligns with analytical decision-making in marketing.
resumo: Agrupar observações em grupos é uma das técnicas analíticas de marketing mais comuns. Existem muitos procedimentos de seleção de variáveis disponíveis para agrupamento, e alguns mostraram bom desempenho em estudos de simulação. Infelizmente, os métodos com melhor desempenho muitas vezes falham porque enfatizam o poder de agrupamento de variáveis individuais. Por essa razão, recomendamos extrema cautela ao usar os procedimentos existentes e argumentamos que a enumeração de todos os subconjuntos de variáveis possíveis é uma estratégia preferida. Também abordamos um problema de decisão comum— a seleção do número de clusters— e desenvolvemos um índice que pode ajudar a orientar a seleção conjunta de variáveis e clusters. Por meio de um exemplo empírico, ilustramos o problema de seleção de variáveis e demonstramos o uso do índice proposto para selecionar conjuntamente variáveis e clusters na partição K-means.

Title: Assessing hotel readiness to offer local cuisines: a clustering approach
Authors: Bondzi-Simpson A.; Ayeh J.K.
Abstract: Purpose: The purpose of this paper is to assess the organisational readiness of small and medium scaled hotels to serve indigenous local cuisines and to segment the hotel properties for gastronomic tourism campaigning and destination marketing aims. The study also explores how the concept of organisational readiness relates to menu decision makers’ intentions, perceived benefits and organisational characteristics. Design/methodology/approach: Organisational readiness was measured by three dimensions (culture, climate and capacity). Data were derived from a survey of primary menu decision makers from 187 hotels in Ghana. Using a combination of hierarchical and non-hierarchical (K-means) algorithms, the hotels were clustered into homogenous groups based on the original raw scores of hotel readiness indicators. The resultant cluster solution was then validated and profiled against relevant external variables. Findings: Analyses reveal three clusters which distinguish hotels by the degree of readiness to serve indigenous local dishes. The resultant segments differ by hotel category (star rating) as well as by the job positions and perceptions of primary menu decision makers. Unexpectedly, lower class hotels displayed significantly greater levels of organisational readiness to serve indigenous cuisines than those in the higher class category. Research limitations/implications: The study demonstrates that organisational readiness is related to perceived benefits and intentions. Among others, the findings advance the understanding of organisational readiness in hotels in the context of menu decision-making. Given the need to embed new practices in a fast-changing hospitality environment, insights drawn could also serve as a basis for future research. Generalisability of empirical findings may be limited by the socio-economic context as well as the study’s focus on small and medium scaled hotels. Practical implications: This paper supports hotel businesses in understanding the concept of organisational readiness and its relation to organisational characteristics and menu decision-making. By highlighting the different clusters of hotels, the findings accentuate the need for destination marketers and gastronomic tourism campaigners to target higher classed hotels and draw attention to the potential benefits of serving indigenous cuisines while addressing latent concerns. The results further underscore the role of organisational culture and the necessity for such campaign activities to be directed towards those with ample influence within the hierarchical structures of hotels. Originality/value: This is an initial attempt to examine the application of the organisational readiness concept to menu decision-making in hotels and to explore the implications for segmentation purposes. Further analysis revealed the critical role of organisational culture on menu decision-making patterns. Thus, the paper applies an important element of organisational development theory to the hotel industry and represents a valuable contribution to the scant literature on indigenous cuisines in hotel food service contexts. © 2019, Emerald Publishing Limited.
Keywords: Culinary tourism; Food service; Indigenous dishes; Menus; Organizational readiness; Segmentation
keywords: organisational readiness, market segmentation, menu decision-making, gastronomic tourism, perceived benefits
rationale: The abstract discusses the assessment of organisational readiness in small and medium-sized hotels, focusing on menu decision-making related to indigenous local cuisines. This involves strategic analysis, market segmentation, and understanding perceived benefits, aligning with the definitions under Thinking AI, particularly in market analysis and targeting.
resumo: O objetivo deste artigo é avaliar a prontidão organizacional de hotéis de pequeno e médio porte para servir culinárias locais indígenas e segmentar as propriedades hoteleiras para campanhas de turismo gastronômico e marketing de destinos. O estudo também explora como o conceito de prontidão organizacional se relaciona com as intenções dos tomadores de decisão do menu, benefícios percebidos e características organizacionais. A prontidão organizacional foi medida por três dimensões (cultura, clima e capacidade) e os dados foram obtidos por meio de uma pesquisa com 187 hotéis em Gana. Os hotéis foram agrupados em clusters homogêneos com base nos indicadores de prontidão. As análises revelaram três clusters que distinguem os hotéis pelo grau de prontidão para servir pratos locais indígenas, com hotéis de classe inferior apresentando níveis significativamente maiores de prontidão organizacional do que os de classe superior. O estudo demonstra que a prontidão organizacional está relacionada a benefícios percebidos e intenções, contribuindo para a compreensão da prontidão organizacional no contexto da tomada de decisão sobre menus. As implicações práticas sugerem que os negócios hoteleiros compreendam a prontidão organizacional e sua relação com as características organizacionais e a tomada de decisão sobre menus, destacando a necessidade de direcionar campanhas para hotéis de classe superior e enfatizando os benefícios de servir culinárias indígenas. Este trabalho representa uma contribuição valiosa para a literatura escassa sobre culinárias indígenas em contextos de serviços de alimentação em hotéis.

Title: Analytics in sport marketing
Authors: Mumcu C.; Fried G.
Abstract: The use of analytics has been growing throughout the sport industry. Although the concepts of analytics and big data are frequently used in the sport industry and highlighted in numerous media outlets, sport management students often do not have a strong understanding of why and how analytics are important for their future career, especially as it relates to sport marketing. This case study describes a fictitious student`'s desire to be an intern in the analytics department at Major League Soccer and the student`'s interaction with an industry professional who is an expert on customer relationship management and marketing analytics in the sport industry. The study provides information on how and why analytics are used in sport marketing and how data can be used to make decisions. © 2017 North American Society for Sport Management.
Keywords: Analytics; Segmentation; Sport marketing
keywords: analytics, customer relationship management, marketing analytics, sport marketing, data-driven decisions
rationale: The abstract focuses on the application of analytics in the sport industry, particularly in marketing contexts. It discusses how analytics can inform decision-making and improve understanding of customer relationships, aligning with market analysis and targeting strategies. The emphasis on the interaction with an industry professional also suggests a focus on strategic analysis and competitive advantages, which are key aspects of Thinking AI.
resumo: O uso de análises tem crescido na indústria do esporte. Apesar de os conceitos de análises e big data serem frequentemente mencionados, estudantes de gestão esportiva muitas vezes não compreendem plenamente a importância dessas ferramentas para suas futuras carreiras, especialmente em marketing esportivo. Este estudo de caso descreve o desejo de um estudante fictício de estagiar no departamento de análises da Major League Soccer e sua interação com um profissional da indústria especializado em gestão de relacionamento com clientes e análises de marketing. O estudo fornece informações sobre como e por que as análises são utilizadas no marketing esportivo e como os dados podem ser usados para tomar decisões.

Title: Segmenting and Profiling the Chocolate Consumer: An Emerging Market Perspective
Authors: Sondhi N.; Chawla D.
Abstract: Psychographic segmentation has found higher merit among marketing scholars and practicing managers in designing effective marketing strategies to target and deliver better—especially for indulgence food such as chocolates. Hence, adopting a mixed method approach, 17 attitudinal statements were generated through focus group discussions and were used to segment a sample of 301 urban chocolate consumers. The survey data was subjected to a K-means cluster analysis, and it revealed the existence of three distinct clusters: the innovative national; the conservative patriot; and the global seeker. Chi-square analysis was conducted to profile the three groups. Though the study was exploratory in nature, the clusters exhibited such distinct buying patterns that the results hold tremendous value not only from an academic perspective but also for chocolate manufacturers and retailers. All three groups were buying chocolates for gifting purpose, while the young innovators liked to buy for self-gifts as well. Point of sales display had maximum impact on their purchase decision. The global seeker was buying more foreign brands versus the other two, who bought chocolate brands of national origin. © 2017 Taylor & Francis.
Keywords: adult consumers; Chocolate consumption; cluster analysis; emerging markets; Segmentation
keywords: psychographic segmentation, attitudinal statements, customer understanding, buying patterns, gifting purpose, emotional needs
rationale: The abstract discusses psychographic segmentation and the distinct buying patterns of different consumer groups, which indicates a focus on understanding customer emotions and preferences. The study highlights how different clusters of consumers buy chocolates for various reasons, including gifting and self-gifting, showing an understanding of customer emotional needs. This aligns well with the objectives of Feeling AI, which centers on customer understanding and relationalization.
resumo: A segmentação psicográfica tem se mostrado valiosa para acadêmicos e gestores de marketing na criação de estratégias eficazes, especialmente para alimentos indulgentes como chocolates. Utilizando uma abordagem mista, foram geradas 17 afirmações atitudinais por meio de discussões em grupo e aplicadas a uma amostra de 301 consumidores urbanos de chocolate. A análise de cluster K-means revelou três grupos distintos: o inovador nacional, o patriota conservador e o buscador global. Uma análise qui-quadrado foi realizada para caracterizar os três grupos. Embora o estudo tenha sido exploratório, os padrões de compra distintos observados conferem grande valor tanto acadêmico quanto prático para fabricantes e varejistas de chocolate. Todos os grupos compravam chocolates para presentear, enquanto os jovens inovadores também compravam para se auto-presentear. A exibição no ponto de venda teve o maior impacto na decisão de compra. O buscador global comprava mais marcas estrangeiras em comparação aos outros dois grupos, que preferiam marcas de origem nacional.

Title: Hyundai Motors India Limited: positioning towards market leadership
Authors: Kainth J.; Mathur T.
Abstract: Subject area:: Marketing Management, Product Management, Marketing Strategy. Study level/applicability: Bachelor of Business Studies, MBA, Executive MBA. Case overview: The case throws light on the intensely competitive Indian passenger car market and its unique challenges faced by Hyundai Motors India Limited (HMIL). It tries to capture the evolution of this dynamic industry, which is characterized by regular product launches and re-positioning efforts. The students are expected to assess the performance of HMIL and the success of its positioning efforts through multiple quantitative and qualitative data points given in the case. The students need to come up with recommendations whether, amidst intense competition, Government regulations and changing consumer expectations, HMIL should launch new products in its portfolio? If, yes, in which segments? And what should be the guiding philosophy behind such product launches? Expected learning outcomes: The case is expected to guide students: 1. in comprehending the various macro-environmental factors that has made India an attractive passenger car market to invest and operate in, to virtually all multinational players across all segments; 2. in analyzing how the passenger car market is segmented in India; 3. in assessing the product-driven segment-wise performance by HMIL specifically and organizations in general and what are its implications on decision-making; this is indicative of the brand portfolio management based on BCG Brand/Product Portfolio Growth Share Matrix; 4. in assessing the impact of re-positioning on the firms performance judged before and after the re-positioning efforts by the firm; 5. in analyzing the market potential of SUVs and MUVs in India and whether HMIL should launch new products/brands for these segments; and 6. in deliberating on the guiding philosophy in new product launches around the concept of “Consumer Perceived Value”. keywords: market analysis, competitive advantages, product launches, consumer expectations, positioning efforts, market segmentation, product-driven performance, new product launches, consumer perceived value

This aligns closely with the Thinking AI category, which involves market analysis and identifying competitive advantages. The need for recommendations on product launches further indicates a strategic approach to targeting and market segmentation.
resumo: O caso aborda o competitivo mercado indiano de automóveis de passageiros e os desafios únicos enfrentados pela Hyundai Motors India Limited (HMIL). Ele captura a evolução dessa indústria dinâmica, caracterizada por lançamentos frequentes de produtos e esforços de reposicionamento. Os alunos devem avaliar o desempenho da HMIL e o sucesso de suas estratégias de posicionamento, utilizando dados quantitativos e qualitativos apresentados no caso. A questão central é se, em meio à intensa concorrência, regulamentações governamentais e mudanças nas expectativas dos consumidores, a HMIL deve lançar novos produtos em seu portfólio, e, em caso afirmativo, em quais segmentos e com que filosofia orientadora. Os resultados esperados incluem a compreensão dos fatores macroambientais que tornam a Índia um mercado atraente para investimentos, a análise da segmentação do mercado de automóveis de passageiros, a avaliação do desempenho segmentado da HMIL, o impacto do reposicionamento no desempenho da empresa, a análise do potencial de mercado de SUVs e MUVs, e a deliberação sobre a filosofia orientadora em lançamentos de novos produtos em torno do conceito de "Valor Percebido pelo Consumidor". Materiais suplementares estão disponíveis apenas para educadores.

Title: A strategic framework for artificial intelligence in marketing
Authors: Huang M.-H.; Rust R.T.
Abstract: The authors develop a three-stage framework for strategic marketing planning, incorporating multiple artificial intelligence (AI) benefits: mechanical AI for automating repetitive marketing functions and activities, thinking AI for processing data to arrive at decisions, and feeling AI for analyzing interactions and human emotions. This framework lays out the ways that AI can be used for marketing research, strategy (segmentation, targeting, and positioning, STP), and actions. At the marketing research stage, mechanical AI can be used for data collection, thinking AI for market analysis, and feeling AI for customer understanding. At the marketing strategy (STP) stage, mechanical AI can be used for segmentation (segment recognition), thinking AI for targeting (segment recommendation), and feeling AI for positioning (segment resonance). At the marketing action stage, mechanical AI can be used for standardization, thinking AI for personalization, and feeling AI for relationalization. We apply this framework to various areas of marketing, organized by marketing 4Ps/4Cs, to illustrate the strategic use of AI. © 2020, The Author(s).

rationale: The abstract outlines a framework that incorporates AI in several stages of marketing, specifically highlighting the role of feeling AI in analyzing interactions and human emotions. It emphasizes customer understanding, positioning, and relationalization, which directly align with the definitions provided for feeling AI. Additionally, while mechanical and thinking AI elements are present, the focus on emotional aspects indicates a stronger association with feeling AI.
resumo: Os autores desenvolvem uma estrutura em três etapas para o planejamento estratégico de marketing, incorporando múltiplos benefícios da inteligência artificial (IA): IA mecânica para automatizar funções e atividades repetitivas de marketing, IA pensante para processar dados e tomar decisões, e IA emocional para analisar interações e emoções humanas. Essa estrutura delineia as formas como a IA pode ser utilizada na pesquisa de marketing, estratégia (segmentação, direcionamento e posicionamento, STP) e ações. Na etapa de pesquisa de marketing, a IA mecânica pode ser usada para coleta de dados, a IA pensante para análise de mercado e a IA emocional para compreensão do cliente. Na etapa de estratégia de marketing (STP), a IA mecânica pode ser utilizada para segmentação (reconhecimento de segmentos), a IA pensante para direcionamento (recomendação de segmentos) e a IA emocional para posicionamento (ressonância de segmentos). Na etapa de ação de marketing, a IA mecânica pode ser usada para padronização, a IA pensante para personalização e a IA emocional para relacionalização. Aplicamos essa estrutura a várias áreas de marketing, organizadas pelos 4Ps/4Cs de marketing, para ilustrar o uso estratégico da IA.

Title: Consumption self-control by rationing purchase quantities of virtue and vice
Authors: Wertenbroch K.
Abstract: Consumers' attempts to control their unwanted consumption impulses influence many everyday purchases with broad implications for marketers' pricing policies. Addressing theoreticians and practitioners alike, this paper uses multiple empirical methods to show that consumers voluntarily and strategically ration their purchase quantities of goods that are likely to be consumed on impulse and that therefore may pose self-control problems. For example, many regular smokers buy their cigarettes by the pack, although they could easily afford to buy 10-pack cartons. These smokers knowingly forgo sizable per-unit savings from quantity discounts, which they could realize if they bought cartons; by rationing their purchase quantities, they also self-impose additional transactions costs on marginal consumption, which makes excessive smoking overly difficult and costly. Such strategic self-imposition of constraints is intuitively appealing yet theoretically problematic. The marketing literature lacks operationalizations and empirical tests of such consumption self-control strategies and of their managerial implications. This paper provides experimental evidence of the operation of consumer self-control and empirically illustrates its direct implications for the pricing of consumer goods. Moreover, the paper develops a conceptual frame-work for the design of empirical tests of such self-imposed constraints on consumption in consumer goods markets. Within matched pairs of products, we distinguish relative "virtue" and "vice" goods whose preference ordering changes with whether consumers evaluate immediate or delayed consumption consequences. For example, ignoring long-term health effects, many smokers prefer regular (relative vice) to light (relative virtue) cigarettes, because they prefer the taste of the former. However, ignoring these short-term taste differences, the same smokers prefer light to regular cigarettes when they consider the long-term health effects of smoking. These preference orders can lead to dynamically inconsistent consumption choices by consumers whose tradeoffs between the immediate and delayed consequences of consumption depend on the time lag between purchase and consumption. This creates a potential self-control problem, because these consumers will be tempted to overconsume the vices they have in stock at home. Purchase quantity rationing helps them solve the self-control Problem by limiting their stock and hence their consumption opportunities. Such rationing implies that, per purchase occasion, vice consumers will be less likely than virtue consumers to buy larger quantities in response to unit price reductions such as quantity discounts. We first test this prediction in two laboratory experiments. We then examine the external validity of the results at the retail level with a field survey of quantity discounts and with a scanner data analysis of chain-wide store-level demand across a variety of different pairs of matched vice (regular) and virtue (reduced fat, calorie, or caffeine, etc.) product categories. The analyses of these experimental, field, and scanner data provide strong convergent evidence of a characteristic crossover in demand schedules for relative vices and virtues for categories as diverse as, among others, potato chips, chocolate chip cookies, cream cheese, beer, soft drinks, ice cream and frozen yogurt, chewing gum, coffee, and beef and turkey bologna. Vice consumers' demand increases less in response to price reductions than virtue consumers' demand, although their preferences are not generally weaker for vices than for virtues. Constraints on vice purchases are self-imposed and strategic rather than driven by simple preferences. We suggest that rationing their vice inventories at the point of purchase allows consumers to limit subsequent consumption. As a result of purchase quantity rationing, however, vice buyers forgo savings from price reductions through quantity discounts, effectively paying price premiums for the opportunity to engage in self-control. Thus, purchase quantity rationing vice consumers are relatively price insensitive. From a managerial and public policy perspective, our findings should offer marketing practitioners in many consumer goods industries new opportunities to increase profits through segmentation and price discrimination based on consumer self-control. They can charge premium prices for small sizes of vices, relative to the corresponding quantity discounts for virtues. Virtue consumers, on the other hand, will buy larger amounts even when quantity discounts are relatively shallow. A key conceptual contribution of this paper lies in showing how marketing researchers can investigate a whole class of strategic self-constraining consumer behaviors empirically. Moreover, this research is the first to extend previous, theoretical work on impulse control by empirically demonstrating its broader implications for marketing decision making.

resumo: Os esforços dos consumidores para controlar seus impulsos de consumo indesejado influenciam muitas compras do dia a dia, com amplas implicações para as políticas de preços dos profissionais de marketing. Este artigo utiliza múltiplos métodos empíricos para mostrar que os consumidores racionam voluntariamente e de forma estratégica as quantidades de produtos que provavelmente serão consumidos por impulso, o que pode gerar problemas de autocontrole. Por exemplo, muitos fumantes regulares compram cigarros por maço, mesmo podendo comprar caixas com 10 maços, renunciando a economias por descontos de quantidade. Ao racionar suas compras, eles impõem custos adicionais ao consumo marginal, dificultando o excesso de consumo. A literatura de marketing carece de operacionalizações e testes empíricos dessas estratégias de autocontrole e suas implicações gerenciais. O artigo fornece evidências experimentais do autocontrole do consumidor e ilustra suas implicações diretas para a precificação de bens de consumo. Além disso, desenvolve um quadro conceitual para testes empíricos dessas restrições autoimpostas nos mercados de bens de consumo. Dentro de pares de produtos, distinguimos bens de "virtude" e "vice", cuja preferência muda dependendo da avaliação das consequências do consumo imediato ou tardio. Os consumidores de vícios tendem a comprar menores quantidades em resposta a reduções de preço do que os consumidores de virtudes. Os dados experimentais, de campo e de scanner fornecem evidências convergentes de uma característica de cruzamento nas demandas por vícios e virtudes. Os consumidores de vícios são menos sensíveis a preços, pois racionar suas compras permite limitar o consumo subsequente. Nossos achados oferecem novas oportunidades para os profissionais de marketing aumentarem os lucros por meio de segmentação e discriminação de preços com base no autocontrole do consumidor.

Title: Discovering recency, frequency, and monetary (RFM) sequential patterns from customers' purchasing data
Authors: Chen Y.-L.; Kuo M.-H.; Wu S.-Y.; Tang K.
Abstract: In response to the thriving development in electronic commerce (EC), many on-line retailers have developed Web-based information systems to handle enormous amounts of transactions on the Internet. These systems can automatically capture data on the browsing histories and purchasing records of individual customers. This capability has motivated the development of data-mining applications. Sequential pattern mining (SPM) is a useful data-mining method to discover customers' purchasing patterns over time. We incorporate the recency, frequency, and monetary (RFM) concept presented in the marketing literature to define the RFM sequential pattern and develop a novel algorithm for generating all RFM sequential patterns from customers' purchasing data. Using the algorithm, we propose a pattern segmentation framework to generate valuable information on customer purchasing behavior for managerial decision-making. Extensive experiments are carried out, using synthetic datasets and a transactional dataset collected by a retail chain in Taiwan, to evaluate the proposed algorithm and empirically demonstrate the benefits of using RFM sequential patterns in analyzing customers' purchasing data. © 2009 Elsevier B.V. All rights reserved.
Keywords: Constraint-based mining; RFM; Segmentation; Sequential pattern
keywords: data-mining, purchasing patterns, RFM sequential patterns, transactional dataset, data capture
rationale: The abstract discusses the development of Web-based information systems to handle transactions and capture customer data, specifically focusing on sequential pattern mining to analyze purchasing behavior. This aligns with the Mechanical AI category, which emphasizes data collection and segmentation. The use of algorithms to generate RFM sequential patterns further indicates a focus on automating processes related to identifying customer preference patterns.
resumo: Em resposta ao crescimento do comércio eletrônico, muitos varejistas online desenvolveram sistemas de informação baseados na web para gerenciar grandes volumes de transações na Internet. Esses sistemas capturam automaticamente dados sobre os históricos de navegação e registros de compras dos clientes. Essa capacidade motivou o desenvolvimento de aplicações de mineração de dados. A mineração de padrões sequenciais (SPM) é um método útil para descobrir os padrões de compra dos clientes ao longo do tempo. Incorporamos o conceito de recência, frequência e valor monetário (RFM) da literatura de marketing para definir o padrão sequencial RFM e desenvolver um novo algoritmo para gerar todos os padrões sequenciais RFM a partir dos dados de compras dos clientes. Usando o algoritmo, propomos uma estrutura de segmentação de padrões para gerar informações valiosas sobre o comportamento de compra dos clientes para a tomada de decisões gerenciais. Experimentos extensivos foram realizados, utilizando conjuntos de dados sintéticos e um conjunto de dados transacionais coletados por uma rede de varejo em Taiwan, para avaliar o algoritmo proposto e demonstrar empiricamente os benefícios do uso de padrões sequenciais RFM na análise dos dados de compras dos clientes. © 2009 Elsevier B.V. Todos os direitos reservados.

Title: New approach to customer segmentation based on changes in customer value
Authors: Hosseini M.; Shabani M.
Abstract: In today’s fast moving world of marketing from product-orientation to customer-orientation, the management of customer treatment can be seen as a key to achieve revenue growth and profitability. Knowledge of customer behavior can help marketing managers re-evaluate their strategies with the customers and plan to improve and expand their application of the most effective strategies. B2B or business customers are more complex, their buying process is more complicated and their sales value is greater. The business marketers usually prefer to cooperate with fewer but larger buyers than the final consumer marketer. As a business transaction requires more decision makings and more professional buying effort than the consumer market does, the efficient relationship with business customers is of paramount importance. Most customer segmentation approaches based on customer value fail to account for the factor of time and the trend of value changes in their analysis. In this article, we classify customers based on their value using the RFM model and K-means clustering method. Then, an assessment of changes over several periods of time is carried out. The originality of this research lies in its incorporation of time and trend of customer value changes in improving the accuracy of predictions based on the past behavior of customers. For this purpose, we used the POS customer transactions. © 2015 Macmillan Publishers Ltd.
Keywords: Customer lifetime value; RFM model; Segmentation; Temporal data mining
keywords: customer behavior, marketing managers, strategies, customer segmentation, RFM model, K-means clustering, assessment, predictions, customer transactions
rationale: The abstract discusses the classification of customers based on their value using the RFM model and K-means clustering method, which aligns with market analysis and targeting strategies. The focus on understanding customer behavior and re-evaluating marketing strategies indicates a strategic analytical approach inherent in Thinking AI. Additionally, the research emphasizes improving the accuracy of predictions based on past customer behavior, which correlates with market analysis and targeting best practices.
resumo: No mundo do marketing atual, que evolui de uma orientação para produtos para uma orientação para o cliente, a gestão do tratamento ao cliente é fundamental para o crescimento da receita e a lucratividade. Compreender o comportamento do cliente ajuda os gerentes de marketing a reavaliar suas estratégias e a planejar melhorias. Os clientes B2B são mais complexos, com um processo de compra mais complicado e um valor de venda maior. Os profissionais de marketing B2B geralmente preferem cooperar com menos compradores, mas de maior porte. Como as transações comerciais exigem mais decisões e um esforço de compra mais profissional, manter um relacionamento eficiente com os clientes empresariais é crucial. Muitas abordagens de segmentação de clientes baseadas em valor não consideram o fator tempo e as mudanças de valor em suas análises. Este artigo classifica os clientes com base em seu valor utilizando o modelo RFM e o método de agrupamento K-means, além de avaliar as mudanças ao longo de vários períodos. A originalidade da pesquisa reside na incorporação do tempo e da tendência das mudanças de valor do cliente para melhorar a precisão das previsões com base no comportamento passado dos clientes, utilizando transações de clientes em PDV.

Title: Uplift modeling and its implications for B2B customer churn prediction: A segmentation-based modeling approach
Authors: De Caigny A.; Coussement K.; Verbeke W.; Idbenjra K.; Phan M.
Abstract: Business-to-business (B2B) customer retention relies heavily on analytics and predictive modeling to support decision making. Given this, we introduce uplift modeling as a relevant prescriptive analytics tool. In particular, the uplift logit leaf model offers a segmentation-based algorithm that combines predictive performance with interpretability. Applied to a real-world data set of 6432 customers of a European software provider, the uplift logit leaf model achieves superior performance relative to three other popular uplift models in our study. The accessibility of output gained from the uplift logit leaf model also is showcased with a case study, which reveals relevant managerial insights. This new tool thus delivers novel insights in the form of customized, global, and segment-level visualizations that are especially pertinent to industrial marketing settings. Overall, the findings affirm the viability of uplift modeling for improving decisions related to B2B customer retention management. © 2021 Elsevier Inc.
Keywords: Churn prediction; Customer retention; Interpretability; Segmentation-based modeling; Uplift modeling; Visualization
keywords: customer retention, analytics, predictive modeling, uplift modeling, segmentation, managerial insights
rationale: The abstract discusses the application of uplift modeling and predictive analytics to improve B2B customer retention decisions. It emphasizes the importance of market analysis and segmentation-based algorithms, which aligns with the Thinking AI category focused on market analysis and targeting. The findings provide insights that can enhance decision-making processes, indicating a strategic analytical application rather than purely mechanical or emotional.
resumo: A retenção de clientes em negócios B2B depende fortemente de análises e modelagem preditiva para apoiar a tomada de decisões. Neste contexto, apresentamos a modelagem de uplift como uma ferramenta analítica prescritiva relevante. Em particular, o modelo de folha logit de uplift oferece um algoritmo baseado em segmentação que combina desempenho preditivo com interpretabilidade. Aplicado a um conjunto de dados real de 6432 clientes de um provedor de software europeu, o modelo de folha logit de uplift alcança desempenho superior em relação a outros três modelos de uplift populares em nosso estudo. A acessibilidade dos resultados obtidos com o modelo de folha logit de uplift também é demonstrada por meio de um estudo de caso, que revela insights gerenciais relevantes. Esta nova ferramenta, portanto, fornece insights inovadores na forma de visualizações personalizadas, globais e em nível de segmento, que são especialmente pertinentes a ambientes de marketing industrial. No geral, os resultados confirmam a viabilidade da modelagem de uplift para melhorar as decisões relacionadas à gestão de retenção de clientes B2B.

Title: Assessing hotel readiness to offer local cuisines: a clustering approach
Authors: Bondzi-Simpson A.; Ayeh J.K.
Abstract: Purpose: The purpose of this paper is to assess the organisational readiness of small and medium scaled hotels to serve indigenous local cuisines and to segment the hotel properties for gastronomic tourism campaigning and destination marketing aims. The study also explores how the concept of organisational readiness relates to menu decision makers’ intentions, perceived benefits and organisational characteristics. Design/methodology/approach: Organisational readiness was measured by three dimensions (culture, climate and capacity). Data were derived from a survey of primary menu decision makers from 187 hotels in Ghana. Using a combination of hierarchical and non-hierarchical (K-means) algorithms, the hotels were clustered into homogenous groups based on the original raw scores of hotel readiness indicators. The resultant cluster solution was then validated and profiled against relevant external variables. Findings: Analyses reveal three clusters which distinguish hotels by the degree of readiness to serve indigenous local dishes. The resultant segments differ by hotel category (star rating) as well as by the job positions and perceptions of primary menu decision makers. Unexpectedly, lower class hotels displayed significantly greater levels of organisational readiness to serve indigenous cuisines than those in the higher class category. Research limitations/implications: The study demonstrates that organisational readiness is related to perceived benefits and intentions. Among others, the findings advance the understanding of organisational readiness in hotels in the context of menu decision-making. Given the need to embed new practices in a fast-changing hospitality environment, insights drawn could also serve as a basis for future research. Generalisability of empirical findings may be limited by the socio-economic context as well as the study’s focus on small and medium scaled hotels. Practical implications: This paper supports hotel businesses in understanding the concept of organisational readiness and its relation to organisational characteristics and menu decision-making. By highlighting the different clusters of hotels, the findings accentuate the need for destination marketers and gastronomic tourism campaigners to target higher classed hotels and draw attention to the potential benefits of serving indigenous cuisines while addressing latent concerns. The results further underscore the role of organisational culture and the necessity for such campaign activities to be directed towards those with ample influence within the hierarchical structures of hotels. Originality/value: This is an initial attempt to examine the application of the organisational readiness concept to menu decision-making in hotels and to explore the implications for segmentation purposes. Further analysis revealed the critical role of organisational culture on menu decision-making patterns. Thus, the paper applies an important element of organisational development theory to the hotel industry and represents a valuable contribution to the scant literature on indigenous cuisines in hotel food service contexts. © 2019, Emerald Publishing Limited.
Keywords: Culinary tourism; Food service; Indigenous dishes; Menus; Organizational readiness; Segmentation
keywords: organisational readiness, market segmentation, menu decision-making, gastronomic tourism, perceived benefits
rationale: The abstract discusses the assessment of organisational readiness in small and medium-sized hotels, focusing on menu decision-making related to indigenous local cuisines. This involves strategic analysis, market segmentation, and understanding perceived benefits, aligning with the definitions under Thinking AI, particularly in market analysis and targeting.
resumo: O objetivo deste artigo é avaliar a prontidão organizacional de hotéis de pequeno e médio porte para servir culinárias locais indígenas e segmentar as propriedades hoteleiras para campanhas de turismo gastronômico e marketing de destinos. O estudo também explora como o conceito de prontidão organizacional se relaciona com as intenções dos tomadores de decisão do menu, benefícios percebidos e características organizacionais. A prontidão organizacional foi medida por três dimensões (cultura, clima e capacidade) e os dados foram obtidos por meio de uma pesquisa com tomadores de decisão do menu de 187 hotéis em Gana. Os hotéis foram agrupados em categorias homogêneas com base nas pontuações dos indicadores de prontidão. As análises revelaram três grupos que distinguem os hotéis pelo grau de prontidão para servir pratos locais. Os segmentos resultantes diferem pela categoria do hotel (classificação por estrelas) e pelas percepções dos tomadores de decisão do menu. Surpreendentemente, hotéis de classe inferior apresentaram níveis significativamente maiores de prontidão organizacional do que os de classe superior. O estudo demonstra que a prontidão organizacional está relacionada a benefícios percebidos e intenções, avançando a compreensão desse conceito no contexto da tomada de decisão do menu. As implicações práticas sugerem que os negócios hoteleiros compreendam a prontidão organizacional e sua relação com as características organizacionais e a tomada de decisão do menu, enfatizando a necessidade de direcionar campanhas para hotéis de classe superior e destacar os benefícios de servir culinárias indígenas. Este artigo representa uma contribuição valiosa para a literatura escassa sobre culinárias indígenas no contexto de serviços alimentares em hotéis.

Title: Customer segmentation model based on value generation for marketing strategies formulation; [Modelo de segmentação do cliente baseado na criação de valor para a formulação de estratégias de marketing]; [Modelo de segmentación de clientes basado en la generación de valor para la formulación de estrategias de mercadeo]
Authors: Cuadros A.J.; Domínguez V.E.
Abstract: When deciding in which segment to invest or how to distribute the marketing budget, managers generally take risks in making decisions without considering the real impact every client or segment has over organizational profits. In this paper, a segmentation framework is proposed that considers, firstly, the calculation of customer lifetime value, the current value, and client loyalty, and then the building of client segments by self-organized maps. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated with an empirical study in a cane sugar mill where a total of 9 segments of interest were identified for decision making. © 2012 Universidad ICESI. Published by Elsevier España, S.L. All rights reserved.
Keywords: Artificial neural network; Customer value; Segmentation; Self-organized maps
keywords: segmentation, customer lifetime value, client loyalty, market budget, decision making
rationale: The abstract discusses a segmentation framework that involves calculating customer lifetime value and client loyalty, highlighting strategic decision-making in marketing budget allocation. This aligns with the 'Thinking AI' category, which focuses on market analysis and targeting, as it emphasizes the analytical aspect of customer segmentation and profit impacts over traditional methods.
resumo: Quando os gestores decidem em qual segmento investir ou como distribuir o orçamento de marketing, geralmente assumem riscos ao tomar decisões sem considerar o impacto real que cada cliente ou segmento tem sobre os lucros da organização. Este artigo propõe uma estrutura de segmentação que considera, primeiramente, o cálculo do valor do tempo de vida do cliente, o valor atual e a lealdade do cliente, e em seguida, a construção de segmentos de clientes por meio de mapas auto-organizados. A eficácia do método proposto é demonstrada por meio de um estudo empírico em uma usina de açúcar, onde foram identificados um total de 9 segmentos de interesse para a tomada de decisões. © 2012 Universidad ICESI. Title: Managerial applicability of graphical formats to support positioning decisions
Authors: Cornelius B.; Wagner U.; Natter M.
Abstract: Issues of segmentation and positioning have always been at the heart of marketing management. In recent years, much methodological progress has been made in order to carry out these two tasks simultaneously, that is, to combine certain types of clustering algorithms with appropriate multidimensional scaling or unfolding procedures. When trying to provide managers with a tool to support marketing decision-making in segmentation and positioning, the ease of use and the visual quality of results must be emphasized. This paper provides a state-of-the-art review of alternative graphical formats designed to assist strategic management. It focuses on three aspects, namely, (I) representing competitive market structures, (II) illustrating preferences for product attributes, and (III) describing customer heterogeneity at the individual as well as segment-specific levels; this paper also explores the interrelations among these aspects. The benefits and limitations of different approaches are discussed, and graphical examples are provided. Advances in academic research are contrasted with the information requirements of marketing managers. Finally, recommendations on the applicability of these alternatives for practical use are offered, and issues for further research are specified. © Wirtschaftsuniversität Wien, Austria 2010.
Keywords: Graphical formats; Managerial applicability; Multidimensional scaling; Positioning; Segmentation; Targeting; Unfolding
keywords: segmentation, positioning, market analysis, customer preferences, strategic management, competitive market structures, product attributes, customer heterogeneity
rationale: The abstract discusses the methodological advancements in segmentation and positioning within the marketing realm, emphasizing the application of clustering algorithms and multidimensional scaling. It focuses on providing tools for managers to support decision-making, showcasing elements of market analysis and competitive structures, which aligns closely with the definitions under Thinking AI. The paper's emphasis on analyzing customer preferences and competitive market structures further supports its classification in this category.
resumo: As questões de segmentação e posicionamento sempre foram centrais na gestão de marketing. Nos últimos anos, houve um avanço metodológico significativo para realizar essas duas tarefas simultaneamente, combinando algoritmos de agrupamento com procedimentos adequados de escalonamento multidimensional. Ao tentar fornecer aos gestores uma ferramenta para apoiar a tomada de decisões em marketing, é fundamental enfatizar a facilidade de uso e a qualidade visual dos resultados. Este artigo apresenta uma revisão do estado da arte de formatos gráficos alternativos projetados para auxiliar a gestão estratégica, focando em três aspectos: (I) representação das estruturas de mercado competitivo, (II) ilustração das preferências por atributos de produtos e (III) descrição da heterogeneidade dos clientes em níveis individuais e específicos de segmentos. O artigo também explora as inter-relações entre esses aspectos, discute os benefícios e limitações das diferentes abordagens e fornece exemplos gráficos. Os avanços na pesquisa acadêmica são contrastados com as necessidades de informação dos gestores de marketing. Por fim, são oferecidas recomendações sobre a aplicabilidade dessas alternativas para uso prático e especificadas questões para futuras pesquisas.

Title: Segmenting and Profiling the Chocolate Consumer: An Emerging Market Perspective
Authors: Sondhi N.; Chawla D.
Abstract: Psychographic segmentation has found higher merit among marketing scholars and practicing managers in designing effective marketing strategies to target and deliver better—especially for indulgence food such as chocolates. Hence, adopting a mixed method approach, 17 attitudinal statements were generated through focus group discussions and were used to segment a sample of 301 urban chocolate consumers. The survey data was subjected to a K-means cluster analysis, and it revealed the existence of three distinct clusters: the innovative national; the conservative patriot; and the global seeker. Chi-square analysis was conducted to profile the three groups. Though the study was exploratory in nature, the clusters exhibited such distinct buying patterns that the results hold tremendous value not only from an academic perspective but also for chocolate manufacturers and retailers. All three groups were buying chocolates for gifting purpose, while the young innovators liked to buy for self-gifts as well. Point of sales display had maximum impact on their purchase decision. The global seeker was buying more foreign brands versus the other two, who bought chocolate brands of national origin. © 2017 Taylor & Francis.
Keywords: adult consumers; Chocolate consumption; cluster analysis; emerging markets; Segmentation
keywords: psychographic segmentation, attitudinal statements, customer understanding, buying patterns, gifting purpose, emotional needs
rationale: The abstract discusses psychographic segmentation and the distinct buying patterns of different consumer groups, which indicates a focus on understanding customer emotions and preferences. The study highlights how different clusters of consumers buy chocolates for various reasons, including gifting and self-gifting, showing an understanding of customer emotional needs. This aligns well with the objectives of Feeling AI, which centers on customer understanding and relationalization.
resumo: A segmentação psicográfica demonstrou maior relevância entre acadêmicos de marketing e gestores na elaboração de estratégias eficazes para direcionar e oferecer produtos, especialmente alimentos indulgentes como chocolates. Utilizando uma abordagem mista, foram geradas 17 afirmações atitudinais através de discussões em grupo focais, que foram usadas para segmentar uma amostra de 301 consumidores urbanos de chocolate. Os dados da pesquisa foram analisados por meio de uma análise de cluster K-means, revelando a existência de três grupos distintos: o inovador nacional, o patriota conservador e o buscador global. Uma análise qui-quadrado foi realizada para caracterizar os três grupos. Embora o estudo tenha sido exploratório, os clusters apresentaram padrões de compra tão distintos que os resultados têm grande valor tanto do ponto de vista acadêmico quanto para fabricantes e varejistas de chocolate. Todos os três grupos compravam chocolates para presente, enquanto os jovens inovadores também gostavam de comprar para si mesmos. A exibição no ponto de venda teve o maior impacto na decisão de compra. O buscador global comprava mais marcas estrangeiras, em contraste com os outros dois grupos, que preferiam marcas de origem nacional.

Title: Analysis of purchase history data based on a new latent class model for RFM analysis
Authors: Zhang Q.; Yamashita H.; Mikawa K.; Goto M.
Abstract: Recently, it has become easier to make use of various kinds of information on customers (e.g. customers' purchase history), due to the development of information technology. Especially in the marketing field, in fact, many companies try to employ customer segmentation for the services customization which leads to increase customer loyalty and to keep high customer retention. One of the well-known approaches for the customer analysis based on purchase history data is the RFM analysis. The RFM analysis is usually used to segment customers into several groups by using three variables; how long it has been since their last purchase, how many times they purchased, and how much they spent. However, the conventional method of the RFM analysis did not assume a generative model. Therefore, when applying to an actual data set and scoring each index of R, F, M scores, several problems occur. The main problem is that an analyst should arbitrarily decide the threshold for the scores of RFM. On the other hand, in the field of machine learning, the probabilistic latent semantic analysis is widely used for soft clustering. The latent class model enables us to cluster customers into latent classes and to calculate the assignment probabilities of each customer to each latent class. In this paper, we propose a new latent class model for the RFM analysis based on the purchase history data. The proposed model enables to decide the scoring of RFM and segment customers automatically, and the soft clustering approach helps the interpretation of the result. Furthermore, the proposed model takes account of the generation model of RFM scores. From the result of actual data analysis, it became clear that it is possible to extract latent classes that express the statistical characteristics of data well. Given a generative model estimated from the given data, it is also possible to predict future purchase behaviors of customers or to generate virtual data for simulation analysis and make decisions based on the result. We verify the effectiveness of our model by analyzing a real purchase history data of a Japanese major retail company. © 2020 KIIE
Keywords: Latent Class Model; Marketing Segmentation; RFM Analysis
keywords: customer segmentation, RFM analysis, latent class model, purchase behavior, data analysis
rationale: The abstract discusses a new approach to customer segmentation using RFM analysis and a latent class model, which aligns with market analysis and strategic targeting in marketing. The focus on analyzing customer purchase behavior and predicting future actions falls under the scope of Thinking AI, which emphasizes market analysis and targeting. The abstract does not emphasize emotional understanding or mechanical processes, but rather highlights analytical models for customer behavior predictions.
resumo: Recentemente, o uso de informações sobre clientes, como o histórico de compras, tornou-se mais acessível devido ao avanço da tecnologia da informação. Muitas empresas, especialmente no marketing, utilizam a segmentação de clientes para personalizar serviços, aumentando a lealdade e a retenção de clientes. A análise RFM, que segmenta clientes com base em três variáveis (tempo desde a última compra, frequência de compras e valor gasto), é uma abordagem conhecida, mas a metodologia convencional não considera um modelo gerativo, levando a problemas na definição de limiares para as pontuações. Em contraste, a análise semântica latente probabilística é utilizada em aprendizado de máquina para agrupamento suave. Este artigo propõe um novo modelo de classe latente para a análise RFM, que automatiza a segmentação de clientes e a pontuação RFM, além de considerar o modelo gerativo das pontuações. A análise de dados reais demonstrou a capacidade de extrair classes latentes que refletem bem as características estatísticas dos dados, permitindo prever comportamentos de compra futuros e gerar dados virtuais para simulações. A eficácia do modelo foi verificada com dados de uma grande empresa de varejo japonesa.

Title: The value chain of the jumbo squid (Dosidicus gigas) in Mexico: Diagnostic, structural analysis, and scenarios
Authors: Cruz-Escalona V.H.; Moncaleano-Rubio Y.A.; Morales-Bojórquez E.; Arizmendi-Rodríguez D.I.; Pérez-Palafox X.A.; Ornelas-Vargas A.; Payán-Alcacio J.Á.; Urcádiz-Cazares F.J.
Abstract: The value chain for jumbo squid fishery encompasses a process of linking multiple components and actors that generate and promote capitalization of the added value of this fishery product. This study aims to diagnose the value chain for jumbo squid in Mexico using the structural analysis approach, allowing a description of the main actors, and their interactions with the markets, socioeconomic drivers, as well as the influence of different variables in the performance of jumbo squid chain value. The results derived from the structural analysis, six variables (related to the transformation, marketing, and consumption activities) and two actors (producers and academic research) were identified as the most relevant. The competitive advantages and added value could be reached by integrating the aspects related to the most relevant variables and taking appropriate decisions to deal with situations of uncertainty, which can promote weak nodes in the value chain, primarily because of the failures in the commercialization and consumption of jumbo squid. This suggests that efforts should not be concentrated on a single node but should be addressed jointly. Considering that the jumbo squid value chain currently depends on the changing conditions of the fishery, which is marked by production instability, causing uncertainty in the subsequent nodes; the status indicates that a restructuring of the value chain is evident since the market is prone to dismantling or self-regulation over the medium term. © 2024 Elsevier Ltd
