Title: Air India-Vistara merger – maneuvering “Vihaan.AI” through the turbulence
Authors: Chaudhary P.
Abstract: Learning outcomes: The expected learning outcomes are to understand the complexities involved in the integration of two carriers with different business strategies and approaches, the merger of two brands with distinct personas and identities and the confluence of two different cultures; figure out the strategic options in front of the Tata Group and how it can deal with various macro- and micro-level business challenges, defy the financial hiccups and manoeuvre the operational complexities to accomplish mission Vihaan.AI; and develop a pragmatic approach to macro and micro business environmental scanning for making strategic business decisions. Case overview/synopsis: In November 2022, Tata Group, the salt to software conglomerate, announced the merger of Air India (AI) and Vistara. This would lead to the formation of the full-service airline under the brand name “Air India”. The obvious reason behind this was the higher recognition, salience and recall of the brand AI as compared with Vistara in the global market. The Tata Group envisaged the brand AI to be a significant international aviation player with the heritage, persona and ethos of the brand Vistara in the renewed manifestation of AI. To realise these goals, Tata Group laid down an ambitious plan called “Vihaan.AI”, which was aimed at capturing a domestic market share of 30% by 2027. Complexity academic level: This case study can be taught as part of undergraduate- and postgraduate-level management programmes. Supplementary materials: Teaching notes are available for educators only. Subject code: CSS 11: Strategy. © 2023, Emerald Publishing Limited.
Keywords: Aviation industry; Brand management; Business climate; Business environmental analysis; Capacity building and utilisation; Integration; International marketing; Marketing; Marketing strategy; Mergers and acquisitions; Strategic marketing management; Synergy
keywords: integration, business strategies, macro-level business challenges, strategic options, market share, brand recognition, competitive advantages
rationale: The abstract discusses the strategic integration of Air India and Vistara, focusing on understanding market challenges, analyzing competitive advantages, and setting strategic goals for market share. This aligns with the 'Thinking AI' category, which emphasizes market analysis and targeting. The Tata Group's ambitions reflect a strategic approach to understanding and navigating the market landscape rather than just collecting data or focusing on customer emotions.
resumo: Os resultados de aprendizagem esperados incluem a compreensão das complexidades envolvidas na integração de duas empresas com estratégias de negócios diferentes, a fusão de duas marcas com identidades distintas e a confluência de duas culturas diferentes; identificar as opções estratégicas disponíveis para o Grupo Tata e como ele pode enfrentar diversos desafios de negócios em níveis macro e micro, superar dificuldades financeiras e lidar com complexidades operacionais para alcançar a missão Vihaan.AI; e desenvolver uma abordagem pragmática para a análise do ambiente de negócios em níveis macro e micro para a tomada de decisões estratégicas. Em novembro de 2022, o Grupo Tata, um conglomerado que vai do sal ao software, anunciou a fusão da Air India (AI) com a Vistara, resultando na formação de uma companhia aérea de serviço completo sob a marca "Air India". A razão óbvia para isso foi o maior reconhecimento e lembrança da marca AI em comparação com a Vistara no mercado global. O Grupo Tata vislumbrou a marca AI como um importante jogador internacional na aviação, incorporando a herança, persona e ethos da marca Vistara na nova manifestação da AI. Para alcançar esses objetivos, o Grupo Tata estabeleceu um plano ambicioso chamado "Vihaan.AI", com a meta de capturar uma participação de mercado doméstico de 30% até 2027. Este estudo de caso pode ser ensinado em programas de gestão de nível de graduação e pós-graduação.

Title: From mining to meaning: How B2B marketers can leverage text to inform strategy
Authors: Tsao H.-Y.; Campbell C.; Sands S.; Mavrommatis A.
Abstract: Today's marketers are increasingly faced with the need to collect and interpret data to aid firm strategic decision making. At the same time, there has been an explosion of text-based data and numerous advances in big data that enable marketers to mine the collection and aggregation of text. However, for many marketers there is a need to better understand how textual data can go beyond mere descriptive metrics to instead help solve real marketing problems. With this paper, we take a step in this direction. We first review key concepts and terms that are relevant to understanding how text analysis operates, as well as a new development in custom dictionary creation that expands the topics possible with text analysis. Next, we develop the FTTA grid, a new framework that enables text-derived metrics to inform actionable strategies for marketers. We present two real cases demonstrating how the FTTA grid can be employed in action. Finally, we discuss implications for both academics and marketing practitioners. © 2022
Keywords: B2B marketing; Marketing insight; Marketing strategy; Text-analysis
keywords: data interpretation, text-based data, text analysis, actionable strategies, market problems, FTTA grid, custom dictionary
rationale: The abstract discusses the interpretation and analysis of textual data to inform strategic decision-making in marketing. It highlights the development of the FTTA grid, which enables marketers to derive actionable insights from text analysis, suggesting a focus on market analysis and strategic targeting. The emphasis on solving real marketing problems through data-driven insights aligns closely with the Thinking AI category.
resumo: Os profissionais de marketing enfrentam cada vez mais a necessidade de coletar e interpretar dados para auxiliar na tomada de decisões estratégicas. Com o aumento exponencial de dados textuais e avanços em big data, surge a oportunidade de explorar essa coleta e agregação de texto. No entanto, muitos profissionais ainda precisam entender como os dados textuais podem ir além de métricas descritivas e ajudar a resolver problemas reais de marketing. Este artigo revisa conceitos-chave sobre análise de texto e apresenta um novo desenvolvimento na criação de dicionários personalizados. Em seguida, é introduzida a grade FTTA, uma nova estrutura que permite que métricas derivadas de texto informem estratégias acionáveis para os profissionais de marketing, com dois casos reais demonstrando sua aplicação. Por fim, são discutidas as implicações para acadêmicos e profissionais de marketing.

Title: Mentorrd EduTech: charting new territories through social media marketing
Authors: Senecha N.; Srivastava R.
Abstract: Learning outcomes: After studying and analyzing this case, students will be able to: understand and evaluate the integrated marketing communications (IMC) strategy for online businesses; understand and create the various components of an IMC plan; determine the challenges of scaling up a business and how social media marketing can help in that; learn how to assemble the positioning statement of a startup; determine and differentiate the different business models (revenue models); and understand and create the social media marketing strategy. Case overview/synopsis: It was late April 2021, and Mr Srinivas Rao, the co-founder and director of Mentorrd EduTech, India, was contemplating the journey of more than five years. Much had changed since the startup Mentorrd Education Technologies Pvt. Ltd. (Mentorrd EduTech) was launched in 2015. From being an online artificial intelligence (AI)-based tool for analyzing and building resumes, Mentorrd expanded to specialized premium services for career development catering to MBA aspirants from India to international markets. However, during the same time, many problems had also started showing up. The competition had increased, and conversions became difficult. Mentorrd generated 95% of its leads through Google Ads pay per click (PPC) advertising. However, now, the increased competition made PPC costlier, where Mentorrd started at INR 10 per click but was now paying INR 50 per click. The customers also were only limited to searching for keywords; hence, actual lead conversion was minimal. Mentorrd was present on different social media platforms and had developed an audience: LinkedIn (close to 10,000 followers), Facebook (1,600+ followers) and Twitter (numbers), but conversions from there were only contributing to 5% of the total revenue.Mr Rao wondered that with a change in demand from general review services to specialist resume and interview preparation services such as MBA, he would have to develop a sound social media strategy integrated with the current Google Ads usage to reach the audience and generate conversions. He had a limited marketing budget which he wanted to use most effectively but was not sure how to spend across platforms. Complexity academic level: This case can be used as an IMC strategy case for MBA courses in marketing. In a marketing course, the focus should be on components of IMC strategy, customer perception, company positioning and marketing channels. The case can also be applied as a strategy case for courses in entrepreneurship or digital marketing strategy. In an entrepreneurship course, the focus should be on the business model, growth and scaling decisions a startup needs to make to grow the business. In a digital marketing strategy course, the focus should be on social media marketing and search engine marketing decisions and the implications for revenues and profits. The case can also be used in executive-level courses to illustrate IMC, growth and digital marketing strategies for a startup. Supplementary materials: Teaching notes are available for educators only. Subject code: CSS 8: Marketing. © 2022, Emerald Publishing Limited.
Keywords: Digital marketing; Marketing mix; Marketing strategy; Sales promotions; Social marketing; Social media strategy
keywords: customer understanding, positioning, social media marketing strategy, customer perception, company positioning
rationale: The abstract discusses the challenges faced by Mentorrd EduTech in understanding its customer base and developing an effective marketing strategy. The emphasis on creating a social media marketing strategy and understanding customer needs indicates a focus on customer understanding and positioning, aligning well with the Feeling AI category. Additionally, the case aims to help students learn about customer perception and emotional needs, which further supports this classification.
resumo: Resultados de aprendizagem: Após estudar e analisar este caso, os alunos serão capazes de: compreender e avaliar a estratégia de comunicações de marketing integradas (IMC) para negócios online; entender e criar os diversos componentes de um plano de IMC; determinar os desafios de escalar um negócio e como o marketing em mídias sociais pode ajudar nisso; aprender a montar a declaração de posicionamento de uma startup; determinar e diferenciar os diferentes modelos de negócios (modelos de receita); e entender e criar a estratégia de marketing em mídias sociais. Visão geral do caso: No final de abril de 2021, o Sr. Srinivas Rao, cofundador e diretor da Mentorrd EduTech, na Índia, refletia sobre a jornada de mais de cinco anos. Muitas mudanças ocorreram desde o lançamento da Mentorrd Education Technologies Pvt. Ltd. (Mentorrd EduTech) em 2015. De uma ferramenta online baseada em inteligência artificial (IA) para análise e construção de currículos, a Mentorrd expandiu para serviços premium especializados em desenvolvimento de carreira, atendendo aspirantes a MBA da Índia a mercados internacionais. No entanto, ao mesmo tempo, muitos problemas começaram a surgir. A concorrência aumentou e as conversões se tornaram difíceis. A Mentorrd gerava 95% de seus leads por meio de anúncios do Google Ads (PPC). Contudo, a concorrência aumentada tornou o PPC mais caro, onde a Mentorrd começou pagando INR 10 por clique, mas agora pagava INR 50. Os clientes também estavam limitados a buscar palavras-chave; portanto, a conversão real de leads era mínima. A Mentorrd estava presente em diferentes plataformas de mídias sociais e havia desenvolvido uma audiência: LinkedIn (quase 10.000 seguidores), Facebook (mais de 1.600 seguidores) e Twitter (números), mas as conversões a partir daí contribuíam apenas com 5% da receita total. O Sr. Rao se perguntava, com a mudança na demanda de serviços gerais de revisão para serviços especializados de preparação de currículos e entrevistas, como MBA, ele precisaria desenvolver uma estratégia sólida de mídias sociais integrada ao uso atual do Google Ads para alcançar o público e gerar conversões. Ele tinha um orçamento de marketing limitado que queria usar da forma mais eficaz, mas não tinha certeza de como gastar entre as plataformas. Nível acadêmico de complexidade: Este caso pode ser utilizado como um caso de estratégia de IMC para cursos de MBA em marketing. Em um curso de marketing, o foco deve estar nos componentes da estratégia de IMC, percepção do cliente, posicionamento da empresa e canais de marketing. O caso também pode ser aplicado como um caso de estratégia para cursos de empreendedorismo ou estratégia de marketing digital. Em um curso de empreendedorismo, o foco deve estar no modelo de negócios, decisões de crescimento e escalonamento que uma startup precisa tomar para crescer. Em um curso de estratégia de marketing digital, o foco deve estar nas decisões de marketing em mídias sociais e marketing em motores de busca e suas implicações para receitas e lucros. O caso também pode ser utilizado em cursos de nível executivo para ilustrar estratégias de IMC, crescimento e marketing digital para uma startup. Materiais suplementares: Notas de ensino estão disponíveis apenas para educadores. Código do assunto: CSS 8: Marketing. © 2022, Emerald Publishing Limited.

Title: The Prevalence of Market Segmentation Research in the Tourism Industry in Africa
Authors: Visser H.
Abstract: Despite the benefits that market segmentation could provide to marketers, it is uncertain to what extend market segmentation research informs decisions about marketing strategy in the tourism industry in Africa. The purpose of this paper is to appraise the incidence of market segmentation research in this context. Market segmentation is used to demarcate a broad market into smaller segments to enable the formulation of marketing strategies based on segment needs. A review of journal articles with market segmentation in the tourism industry in the African context as a focus area is provided. While research in this context is available, recommendations are made about possible market segmentation research focus areas in the tourism industry in an African context. © 2021
Keywords: African context; market segmentation; Marketing strategy; research; tourism industry
keywords: market segmentation, marketing strategy, tourism industry, research, recommendations
rationale: The abstract discusses the appraisal of market segmentation research in informing marketing strategy specifically within the tourism industry in Africa. It emphasizes analyzing existing literature and making recommendations for future research focus areas, which aligns closely with the 'Market analysis' and 'Targeting' aspects of Thinking AI. The focus is primarily on strategic analysis rather than emotional understanding or automated processes.
resumo: Apesar dos benefícios que a segmentação de mercado pode oferecer aos profissionais de marketing, não está claro até que ponto a pesquisa em segmentação de mercado informa as decisões sobre a estratégia de marketing na indústria do turismo na África. O objetivo deste artigo é avaliar a incidência da pesquisa em segmentação de mercado nesse contexto. A segmentação de mercado é utilizada para demarcar um mercado amplo em segmentos menores, permitindo a formulação de estratégias de marketing com base nas necessidades dos segmentos. É fornecida uma revisão de artigos de periódicos com foco na segmentação de mercado na indústria do turismo no contexto africano. Embora haja pesquisas disponíveis nesse contexto, são feitas recomendações sobre possíveis áreas de foco para pesquisas em segmentação de mercado na indústria do turismo em um contexto africano. © 2021

Title: Implementing big data analytics in marketing departments: Mixing organic and administered approaches to increase data-driven decision making
Authors: Johnson D.S.; Sihi D.; Muzellec L.
Abstract: This study examines the experience of marketing departments to become fully data-driven decision-making organizations. We evaluate an organic approach of departmental sensemaking and an administered approach by which top management increase the influence of analytics skilled employees. Data collection commenced with 15 depth interviews of marketing and analytics professionals in the US and Europe involved in the implementation of big data analytics (BDA) and was followed by a survey data of 298 marketing and analytics middle management professionals at United States based firms. The survey data supports the logic that BDA sensemaking is initiated by top management and is comprised of four primary activities: external knowledge acquisition, improving digitized data quality, big data analytics experimentation and big data analytics information dissemination. Top management drives progress toward data-driven decision-making by facilitating sensemaking and by increasing the influence of BDA skilled employees. This study suggests that while a shift toward enterprise analytics increases the quality of resource available to the marketing department, this approach could stymie the quality of marketing insights gained from BDA. This study presents a model of how to improve the quality of marketing insights and improve data-driven decision-making. © 2021 by the authors. Licensee MDPI, Basel, Switzerland.
Keywords: Big data analytics implementation; Data driven marketing; Marketing strategy
keywords: data-driven decision-making, big data analytics, market insights, top management, sensemaking, knowledge acquisition
rationale: The abstract discusses the transition of marketing departments towards becoming data-driven organizations, focusing on the role of analytics and top management in improving decision-making processes. It emphasizes market analysis through big data analytics and the importance of acquiring knowledge to enhance marketing insights, aligning with the characteristics of Thinking AI, particularly in market analysis and targeting.
resumo: Este estudo examina a experiência dos departamentos de marketing para se tornarem organizações totalmente orientadas por decisões baseadas em dados. Avaliamos uma abordagem orgânica de compreensão departamental e uma abordagem administrada pela qual a alta administração aumenta a influência de funcionários com habilidades em análise. A coleta de dados começou com 15 entrevistas aprofundadas com profissionais de marketing e análise nos EUA e na Europa envolvidos na implementação de análises de big data (BDA) e foi seguida por uma pesquisa com 298 profissionais de gestão intermediária de marketing e análise em empresas baseadas nos Estados Unidos. Os dados da pesquisa apoiam a lógica de que a compreensão do BDA é iniciada pela alta administração e é composta por quatro atividades principais: aquisição de conhecimento externo, melhoria da qualidade dos dados digitalizados, experimentação em análises de big data e disseminação de informações de análises de big data. A alta administração impulsiona o progresso em direção à tomada de decisões orientada por dados, facilitando a compreensão e aumentando a influência de funcionários com habilidades em BDA. Este estudo sugere que, embora uma mudança em direção à análise empresarial aumente a qualidade dos recursos disponíveis para o departamento de marketing, essa abordagem pode prejudicar a qualidade das percepções de marketing obtidas a partir do BDA. Este estudo apresenta um modelo de como melhorar a qualidade das percepções de marketing e aprimorar a tomada de decisões orientada por dados.

Title: A strategic framework for artificial intelligence in marketing
Authors: Huang M.-H.; Rust R.T.
Abstract: The authors develop a three-stage framework for strategic marketing planning, incorporating multiple artificial intelligence (AI) benefits: mechanical AI for automating repetitive marketing functions and activities, thinking AI for processing data to arrive at decisions, and feeling AI for analyzing interactions and human emotions. This framework lays out the ways that AI can be used for marketing research, strategy (segmentation, targeting, and positioning, STP), and actions. At the marketing research stage, mechanical AI can be used for data collection, thinking AI for market analysis, and feeling AI for customer understanding. At the marketing strategy (STP) stage, mechanical AI can be used for segmentation (segment recognition), thinking AI for targeting (segment recommendation), and feeling AI for positioning (segment resonance). At the marketing action stage, mechanical AI can be used for standardization, thinking AI for personalization, and feeling AI for relationalization. We apply this framework to various areas of marketing, organized by marketing 4Ps/4Cs, to illustrate the strategic use of AI. © 2020, The Author(s).
Keywords: 4Cs; 4Ps; Artificial intelligence; Feeling AI; Machine learning; Marketing strategy; Mechanical AI; Personalization; Positioning; Relationalization; Segmentation; Standardization; Strategic AI marketing; Targeting; Thinking AI
keywords: emotions, customer understanding, relationalization, positioning
rationale: The abstract outlines a framework that incorporates AI in several stages of marketing, specifically highlighting the role of feeling AI in analyzing interactions and human emotions. It emphasizes customer understanding, positioning, and relationalization, which directly align with the definitions provided for feeling AI. Additionally, while mechanical and thinking AI elements are present, the focus on emotional aspects indicates a stronger association with feeling AI.
resumo: Os autores desenvolvem um framework de três etapas para o planejamento estratégico de marketing, incorporando múltiplos benefícios da inteligência artificial (IA): IA mecânica para automatizar funções e atividades de marketing repetitivas, IA pensante para processar dados e tomar decisões, e IA emocional para analisar interações e emoções humanas. Este framework descreve como a IA pode ser utilizada para pesquisa de marketing, estratégia (segmentação, direcionamento e posicionamento, STP) e ações. Na fase de pesquisa de marketing, a IA mecânica pode ser usada para coleta de dados, a IA pensante para análise de mercado e a IA emocional para compreensão do cliente. Na fase de estratégia de marketing (STP), a IA mecânica pode ser usada para segmentação (reconhecimento de segmentos), a IA pensante para direcionamento (recomendação de segmentos) e a IA emocional para posicionamento (ressonância de segmentos). Na fase de ação de marketing, a IA mecânica pode ser usada para padronização, a IA pensante para personalização e a IA emocional para relacionalização. Aplicamos esse framework a várias áreas de marketing, organizadas pelos 4Ps/4Cs do marketing, para ilustrar o uso estratégico da IA.

Title: LRFMP model for customer segmentation in the grocery retail industry: a case study
Authors: Peker S.; Kocyigit A.; Eren P.E.
Abstract: Purpose: The purpose of this paper is to propose a new RFM model called length, recency, frequency, monetary and periodicity (LRFMP) for classifying customers in the grocery retail industry; and to identify different customer segments in this industry based on the proposed model. Design/methodology/approach: This study combines the LRFMP model and clustering for customer segmentation. Real-life data from a grocery chain operating in Turkey is used. Three cluster validation indices are used for optimizing the number of groups of customers and K-means algorithm is employed to cluster customers. First, attributes of the LRFMP model are extracted for each customer, and then based on LRFMP model features, customers are segmented into different customer groups. Finally, identified customer segments are profiled based on LRFMP characteristics and for each customer profile, unique CRM and marketing strategies are recommended. Findings: The results show that there are five different customer groups and based on LRFMP characteristics, they are profiled as: “high-contribution loyal customers,” “low-contribution loyal customers,” “uncertain customers,” “high-spending lost customers” and “low-spending lost customers.” Practical implications: This research may provide researchers and practitioners with a systematic guideline for effectively identifying different customer profiles based on the LRFMP model, give grocery companies useful insights about different customer profiles, and assist decision makers in developing effective customer relationships and unique marketing strategies, and further allocating resources efficiently. Originality/value: This study contributes to prior literature by proposing a new RFM model, called LRFMP for the customer segmentation and providing useful insights about behaviors of different customer types in the Turkish grocery industry. It is also precious from the point of view that it is one of the first attempts in the literature which investigates the customer segmentation in the grocery retail industry. © 2017, © Emerald Publishing Limited.
Keywords: CRM; Customer relations; Customer segmentation; Grocery retail industry; Marketing strategy; RFM model
keywords: customer segments, CRM, marketing strategies, customer profiles, customer characteristics
rationale: The abstract discusses the identification of different customer segments and profiles based on the LRFMP model, focusing on understanding customer behaviors and needs in the grocery retail industry. This aligns with the Feeling AI category, as it emphasizes customer understanding and the development of unique marketing strategies tailored to specific customer profiles. The insights gained from profiling customers can inform how to meet their emotional needs and wants, which is a central focus of Feeling AI.
resumo: O objetivo deste artigo é propor um novo modelo RFM chamado comprimento, recência, frequência, monetário e periodicidade (LRFMP) para classificar clientes na indústria de varejo de alimentos; e identificar diferentes segmentos de clientes com base no modelo proposto. Este estudo combina o modelo LRFMP e agrupamento para segmentação de clientes, utilizando dados reais de uma rede de supermercados na Turquia. Três índices de validação de cluster são usados para otimizar o número de grupos de clientes, e o algoritmo K-means é empregado para agrupar os clientes. Primeiro, os atributos do modelo LRFMP são extraídos para cada cliente, e então, com base nas características do modelo, os clientes são segmentados em diferentes grupos. Os segmentos de clientes identificados são perfilados com base nas características do LRFMP, e para cada perfil, são recomendadas estratégias únicas de CRM e marketing. Os resultados mostram que existem cinco grupos diferentes de clientes, que são perfilados como: “clientes leais de alta contribuição”, “clientes leais de baixa contribuição”, “clientes incertos”, “clientes perdidos de alto gasto” e “clientes perdidos de baixo gasto”. Esta pesquisa pode fornecer diretrizes sistemáticas para identificar efetivamente diferentes perfis de clientes com base no modelo LRFMP, oferecendo às empresas de alimentos insights úteis sobre os diferentes perfis de clientes e auxiliando os tomadores de decisão no desenvolvimento de relacionamentos eficazes com os clientes e estratégias de marketing únicas, além de alocar recursos de forma eficiente. Este estudo contribui para a literatura anterior ao propor um novo modelo RFM, chamado LRFMP, para a segmentação de clientes e fornecer insights úteis sobre os comportamentos de diferentes tipos de clientes na indústria de alimentos turca. É também valioso por ser uma das primeiras tentativas na literatura a investigar a segmentação de clientes na indústria de varejo de alimentos.

Title: Think with me, or think for me? On the future role of artificial intelligence in marketing strategy formulation
Authors: Eriksson T.; Bigi A.; Bonera M.
Abstract: Purpose: This paper explores if and how Artificial Intelligence can contribute to marketing strategy formulation. Design/methodology/approach: Qualitative research based on exploratory in-depth interviews with industry experts currently working with artificial intelligence tools. Findings: Key themes include: (1) Importance of AI in strategic marketing decision management; (2) Presence of AI in strategic decision management; (3) Role of AI in strategic decision management; (4) Importance of business culture for the use of AI; (5) Impact of AI on the business’ organizational model. A key consideration is a “creative-possibility perspective,” highlighting the future potential to use AI not only for rational but also for creative thinking purposes. Research limitations/implications: This work is focused only on strategy creation as a deliberate process. For this, AI can be used as an effective response to the external contingencies of high volumes of data and uncertain environmental conditions, as well as being an effective response to the external contingencies of limited managerial cognition. A key future consideration is a “creative-possibility perspective.” Practical implications: A practical extension of the Gartner Analytics Ascendancy Model (Maoz, 2013). Originality/value: This paper aims to contribute knowledge relating to the role of AI in marketing strategy formulation and explores the potential avenues for future use of AI in the strategic marketing process. This is explored through the lens of contingency theory, and additionally, findings are expressed using the Gartner analytics ascendancy model. © 2020, Emerald Publishing Limited.
Keywords: AI; Artificial intelligence; Creativity; Marketing strategy; Rationality; TQM/Marketing synergy
keywords: Artificial Intelligence, marketing strategy, strategic decision management, data, creative thinking, organizational model
rationale: The abstract discusses the role of Artificial Intelligence in marketing strategy formulation, focusing on strategic decision management and how AI can assist in responding to external data contingencies. This aligns closely with the 'Thinking AI' category, particularly in the context of market analysis and targeting, as it emphasizes the importance of AI in making strategic marketing decisions and leveraging data for competitive advantage.
resumo: Este artigo explora se e como a Inteligência Artificial pode contribuir para a formulação de estratégias de marketing. A pesquisa qualitativa foi baseada em entrevistas exploratórias com especialistas da indústria que trabalham com ferramentas de inteligência artificial. Os principais temas incluem: (1) Importância da IA na gestão de decisões estratégicas de marketing; (2) Presença da IA na gestão de decisões estratégicas; (3) Papel da IA na gestão de decisões estratégicas; (4) Importância da cultura empresarial para o uso da IA; (5) Impacto da IA no modelo organizacional da empresa. Uma consideração chave é a "perspectiva de possibilidade criativa", que destaca o potencial futuro de usar a IA não apenas para fins racionais, mas também para o pensamento criativo. Este trabalho se concentra apenas na criação de estratégias como um processo deliberado, onde a IA pode ser uma resposta eficaz às contingências externas de altos volumes de dados e condições ambientais incertas, além de ser uma resposta eficaz às limitações da cognição gerencial. As implicações práticas incluem uma extensão prática do Modelo de Ascendência Analítica da Gartner. Este artigo visa contribuir com conhecimento sobre o papel da IA na formulação de estratégias de marketing e explora as potenciais avenidas para o uso futuro da IA no processo de marketing estratégico, sendo analisado sob a ótica da teoria da contingência.

Title: Marketing ecosystem: An outside-in view for sustainable advantage
Authors: Zhang, JZ; Watson, GF
Abstract: In the modern business environment, consumers are increasingly influenced by megatrends involving marketplace, technology, socioeconomics, geopolitics, and natural environment. Simultaneously, the data and insights that can inform consumer attitudes and behaviors often reside outside of firms' direct control. Consciously incorporating these interdependent factors into firms' decision-making is essential for adaptability and sustainable profitability. Building on the outside-in perspective, we propose that firm strategies should be informed through the lens of the marketing ecosystem that considers the interrelated and dynamic megatrends. By leveraging advances in data and technology, firms can sense-make the marketplace by extracting insights from massive amounts of diverse consumer data with modern-day analytics. By mapping out the megatrends with marketing analytics, firms can 1) more accurately predict consumers' changing preferences and formulate appropriate strategies to engage with them; and 2) become more market-adaptable and competitive in the present and the future. To deliver sustainably compelling value to customers, firms should adopt an ecosystem mindset and cooperate with various stakeholders. A broad-thinking, agile, and humble firm culture can enable the development of more robust outside-in capabilities. We elaborate on the megatrends in the interconnected world of the marketing ecosystem, and propose emerging research directions in each area.
Keywords: Outside-in marketing; Marketing strategy; Unstructured data; Consumer privacy; Socioeconomics; Sustainability
keywords: megatrends, marketplace, data, analytics, consumer preferences, strategies, market-adaptable, competitive
rationale: The abstract discusses how firms can leverage marketing analytics and insights from megatrends to better understand consumer behavior, predict changing preferences, and formulate appropriate strategies. This aligns well with the definitions and examples related to market analysis, targeting, and personalization, which are all under the Thinking AI category.
resumo: No ambiente de negócios moderno, os consumidores são cada vez mais influenciados por megatendências que envolvem o mercado, tecnologia, socioeconomia, geopolítica e meio ambiente. Os dados e insights que podem informar as atitudes e comportamentos dos consumidores frequentemente estão fora do controle direto das empresas. Incorporar conscientemente esses fatores interdependentes na tomada de decisões das empresas é essencial para a adaptabilidade e a lucratividade sustentável. Com base na perspectiva de fora para dentro, propomos que as estratégias das empresas devem ser informadas através da lente do ecossistema de marketing, que considera as megatendências inter-relacionadas e dinâmicas. Ao aproveitar os avanços em dados e tecnologia, as empresas podem interpretar o mercado extraindo insights de grandes volumes de dados diversos dos consumidores com análises modernas. Mapeando as megatendências com análises de marketing, as empresas podem 1) prever com mais precisão as mudanças nas preferências dos consumidores e formular estratégias adequadas para se engajar com eles; e 2) se tornar mais adaptáveis ao mercado e competitivas no presente e no futuro. Para oferecer um valor sustentável e atraente aos clientes, as empresas devem adotar uma mentalidade de ecossistema e cooperar com várias partes interessadas. Uma cultura empresarial ampla, ágil e humilde pode permitir o desenvolvimento de capacidades mais robustas de fora para dentro. Elaboramos sobre as megatendências no mundo interconectado do ecossistema de marketing e propomos direções emergentes de pesquisa em cada área.

Title: The relationship between marketing strategies and performance in an economic crisis
Authors: Köksal M.H.; Özgül E.
Abstract: Purpose - To examine how companies are affected by economic crises, to assess the effects of marketing strategies on company performance in such conditions, and to identify those that can help companies to maintain successful performance despite turbulence in the operational environment. Design/methodology/approach - A structured questionnaire contained questions relating to 21 marketing strategies, associated with the elements of the marketing mix, plus a "general marketing strategies" category. It was completed by 172 Turkish companies, drawn from a national frame of 1,000. Data were analysed by factor analysis, with performance criteria set as the dependent variable. Results are reported for each of the elements of the marketing mix. Findings - Companies that modify their strategies appropriately can maintain or improve their performance in times of crisis. Conclusions and recommendations identify the strategic changes most likely to achieve that outcome, measured mainly in terms of sales, market share and profitability. Research limitations/implications - Subjective measures of performance were used because of practical obstacles to obtaining objective financial data from the sample, which would have severely reduced the response rate. Future studies should include such data in the analysis. They might also cross-index findings by company size, industry sector and market scope, and take account of company resources and skills. Practical implications - The findings provide valuable insights for decision makers and marketing planners in times of economic crisis, specifically in the Turkish context but potentially in general. Originality/value - Adds a specific focus on marketing strategies to existing studies of general measures taken by companies during economic crises.
Keywords: Company performance; Economic cycles; Marketing mix; Marketing strategy; Turkey
keywords: marketing strategies, company performance, economic crises, market share, sales, profitability
rationale: The abstract focuses on how companies can adjust their marketing strategies to maintain or improve performance during economic crises. This aligns closely with the 'Thinking AI' category, particularly in the aspects of market analysis and targeting. The study aims to identify effective strategies and their impact on performance metrics like sales and market share, indicative of strategic analysis rather than automated processes or emotional understanding.
resumo: O objetivo deste estudo é examinar como as empresas são afetadas por crises econômicas, avaliar os efeitos das estratégias de marketing no desempenho das empresas nessas condições e identificar aquelas que podem ajudar as empresas a manter um desempenho bem-sucedido, apesar da turbulência no ambiente operacional. Foi utilizado um questionário estruturado com perguntas sobre 21 estratégias de marketing, relacionadas aos elementos do mix de marketing, além de uma categoria de "estratégias de marketing geral". O questionário foi respondido por 172 empresas turcas, selecionadas de um total nacional de 1.000. Os dados foram analisados por meio de análise fatorial, com critérios de desempenho definidos como variável dependente. Os resultados são apresentados para cada um dos elementos do mix de marketing. As descobertas mostram que as empresas que modificam suas estratégias de maneira apropriada podem manter ou melhorar seu desempenho em tempos de crise. As conclusões e recomendações identificam as mudanças estratégicas mais propensas a alcançar esse resultado, medidas principalmente em termos de vendas, participação de mercado e lucratividade. As limitações da pesquisa incluem o uso de medidas subjetivas de desempenho devido a obstáculos práticos para obter dados financeiros objetivos da amostra, o que teria reduzido severamente a taxa de resposta. Estudos futuros devem incluir esses dados na análise e podem também cruzar os resultados por tamanho da empresa, setor industrial e escopo de mercado, além de considerar os recursos e habilidades da empresa. As implicações práticas das descobertas oferecem insights valiosos para tomadores de decisão e planejadores de marketing em tempos de crise econômica, especificamente no contexto turco, mas potencialmente aplicáveis de forma mais geral. Este estudo acrescenta um foco específico em estratégias de marketing às pesquisas existentes sobre medidas gerais adotadas por empresas durante crises econômicas.

Title: Integrating group Delphi, fuzzy logic and expert systems for marketing strategy development: the hybridisation and its effectiveness
Authors: li S.; Davies B.; Edwards J.; Kinman R.; Duan Y.
Abstract: A hybrid approach for integrating group Delphi, fuzzy logic and expert systems for developing marketing strategies is proposed in this paper. Within this approach, the group Delphi method is employed to help groups of managers undertake SWOT analysis. Fuzzy logic is applied to fuzzify the results of SWOT analysis. Expert systems are utilised to formulate marketing strategies based upon the fuzzified strategic inputs. In addition, guidelines are also provided to help users link the hybrid approach with managerial judgement and intuition. The effectiveness of the hybrid approach has been validated with MBA and MA marketing students. It is concluded that the hybrid approach is more effective in terms of decision confidence, group consensus, helping to understand strategic factors, helping strategic thinking, and coupling analysis with judgement, etc. © 2002, MCB UP Limited
Keywords: Delphi method; Expert systems; Fuzzy logics; Hybrid systems; Marketing planning; Marketing strategy
keywords: group Delphi, SWOT analysis, fuzzy logic, expert systems, marketing strategies, decision confidence, group consensus, strategic thinking
rationale: The abstract discusses a hybrid approach that integrates group Delphi, fuzzy logic, and expert systems to develop marketing strategies through SWOT analysis. The focus on strategic analysis and formulation of marketing strategies aligns closely with the 'Thinking AI' category, particularly in market analysis and targeting. The combination of these methods enhances decision-making and strategic thinking among marketers, indicating a clear application of analytical tools rather than emotional or mechanical processes.
resumo: Este artigo propõe uma abordagem híbrida para integrar o método Delphi em grupo, lógica fuzzy e sistemas especialistas no desenvolvimento de estratégias de marketing. Nessa abordagem, o método Delphi em grupo é utilizado para auxiliar grupos de gerentes a realizar análises SWOT. A lógica fuzzy é aplicada para fuzzificar os resultados da análise SWOT. Sistemas especialistas são utilizados para formular estratégias de marketing com base nas entradas estratégicas fuzzificadas. Além disso, são fornecidas diretrizes para ajudar os usuários a vincular a abordagem híbrida ao julgamento e à intuição gerenciais. A eficácia da abordagem híbrida foi validada com alunos de MBA e MA em marketing. Conclui-se que a abordagem híbrida é mais eficaz em termos de confiança nas decisões, consenso do grupo, compreensão de fatores estratégicos, estímulo ao pensamento estratégico e conexão entre análise e julgamento, entre outros.

Title: Brand positivity and competitive effects on the evaluation of brand extensions
Authors: Kapoor H.; Heslop L.A.
Abstract: The dominant approach in brand-extension research has focused on the role of fit in the extension evaluation process. Overemphasis on fit has resulted in research designs that involve singular evaluation of the extension without considering how competing brands in the target category might affect the evaluation of brand extensions. Singular evaluations are known to result in brand positivity effects; that is, brand extensions are evaluated more favorably than is warranted. This research finds that singular evaluations do indeed lead to brand positivity effects. However, brand positivity effects are mitigated when respondents were provided with competitive information along with target-category structure and comparative/non-comparative brand positioning statements. Results also suggest that parent brand-extension fit, though an important determinant of an extension's assessment, plays a less critical role in a comparative evaluation context when an extension's brand strength is accounted for in relation to its competition in the target category. Therefore, the findings stress the importance of both competition and parent-brand fit in making informed positioning decisions and more realistic predictions of extension success. The research demonstrates when, how and to what extent comparative evaluations result in lower extension ratings and provides managerial strategies to introduce an extension effectively. © 2009 Elsevier B.V. All rights reserved.
Keywords: Brand extensions; Branding; Decision making; Experimental design; Extension evaluation; Market analysis and response; Marketing strategy
keywords: brand-extension, competitive information, comparative evaluations, brand positioning, parent brand fit
rationale: The abstract discusses the evaluation process of brand extensions and how competition affects these evaluations. It highlights the importance of market analysis by considering competitive information and positioning strategies, which aligns closely with the Thinking AI category focused on market analysis and targeting.
resumo: A pesquisa sobre extensão de marca tem se concentrado no papel do ajuste na avaliação da extensão. A ênfase excessiva no ajuste resultou em designs de pesquisa que avaliam a extensão de forma isolada, sem considerar como marcas concorrentes na categoria-alvo podem afetar essa avaliação. Avaliações isoladas tendem a gerar efeitos de positividade da marca, ou seja, as extensões são avaliadas de forma mais favorável do que merecem. Este estudo confirma que avaliações isoladas realmente levam a efeitos de positividade da marca, mas esses efeitos são atenuados quando os respondentes recebem informações sobre a concorrência, estrutura da categoria-alvo e declarações de posicionamento de marca comparativas/não comparativas. Os resultados sugerem que o ajuste entre a marca-mãe e a extensão, embora seja um determinante importante na avaliação de uma extensão, desempenha um papel menos crítico em um contexto de avaliação comparativa quando a força da marca da extensão é considerada em relação à concorrência na categoria-alvo. Assim, as descobertas ressaltam a importância tanto da concorrência quanto do ajuste da marca-mãe na tomada de decisões de posicionamento informadas e previsões mais realistas sobre o sucesso da extensão. A pesquisa demonstra quando, como e em que medida as avaliações comparativas resultam em classificações mais baixas para extensões e fornece estratégias gerenciais para introduzir uma extensão de forma eficaz.

Title: The impact of outcome, competency and affect on service referral
Authors: Johnson M.; Zinkhan G.M.; Ayala G.S.
Abstract: Proposes a model to explain consumers' willingness to recommend a service provider. The model considers four predictors of this phenomenon: affect, outcome, competency and courtesy. In a laboratory setting, subjects read and responded to a scenario describing a service encounter of a fictitious individual with a dry cleaner and/or an attorney. The subjects were later asked how likely they were to recommend this service provider to a friend experiencing a similar problem. Separate path analyses were performed to analyze each type of service encounter; and in both scenarios, outcome, competency, courtesy, joy and disgust were found to influence the likelihood that the consumer would recommend a particular service provider. The proposed model accounts for more than 72 percent of the variation in the subjects' decision to recommend. © 1998, MCB UP Limited
Keywords: Consumer behaviour; Marketing strategy; Recommendations; Service quality; Services marketing
keywords: willingness to recommend, affect, joy, disgust, customer emotional needs, service encounter
rationale: The abstract discusses a model that explains consumers' willingness to recommend a service provider, focusing on emotional factors such as joy and disgust as well as other predictors like affect and courtesy. This aligns closely with the 'Feeling AI' category, which emphasizes understanding customer emotions and needs. The analysis of emotional responses and their influence on recommendations indicates a strong focus on customer understanding and relationalization.
resumo: O artigo propõe um modelo para explicar a disposição dos consumidores em recomendar um prestador de serviços. O modelo considera quatro preditores: afeto, resultado, competência e cortesia. Em um ambiente de laboratório, os participantes leram e responderam a um cenário sobre um encontro de serviço de um indivíduo fictício com um lavanderia e/ou um advogado. Posteriormente, foram questionados sobre a probabilidade de recomendar esse prestador de serviços a um amigo em situação semelhante. Análises de caminho separadas foram realizadas para cada tipo de encontro de serviço; em ambos os cenários, resultado, competência, cortesia, alegria e desgosto influenciaram a probabilidade de o consumidor recomendar um prestador específico. O modelo proposto explica mais de 72% da variação na decisão dos participantes de recomendar.

Title: The pharmacist's role in the Egyptian pharmaceutical market
Authors: Taher A.; Stuart E.W.; Hegazy I.
Abstract: Purpose: Pharmaceutical companies' marketing strategies have traditionally targeted only physicians and, more recently, consumers. The purpose of this paper is to explore the role of the pharmacist as prescriber, influencer, switcher, and dispenser of pharmaceutical drugs in one developing country, Egypt. Design/methodology/approach: The authors surveyed pharmacists in Cairo, Egypt. The pharmacists were asked to estimate the percentages of patients who came in with a prescription, with only a box or a recommendation for a medicine and with only symptoms, and whether he/she switched the patient to another medicine. Pharmacies were classified as to the social class of the pharmacy neighborhoods. Cluster analysis was used to further classify pharmacists as "Influencers" and "Non-influencers". Findings: Overall the pharmacists influence 39 percent of all purchase decisions for pharmaceuticals with higher levels of influence in lower social class neighborhoods. Approximately one out of four pharmacists was classified as an Influencer. Practical implications: In developing countries, the pharmacist plays a key role in which medicines patients ultimately purchase. Marketing activities directed toward the pharmacist may provide an important opportunity to maximize the pharmaceutical firms' return on marketing investment. Originality/value: Few studies have looked at the marketing of pharmaceutical drugs in developing countries. This paper is unique in that it examines the role of the pharmacist in these markets, thus providing an important addition to the understanding of the challenges to the industry in these countries and important implications for pharmaceutical marketing strategies. © Emerald Group Publishing Limited.
Keywords: Developing countries; Egypt; Expert power; Influence; Marketing strategy; Pharmaceutical marketing; Pharmaceutical products; Pharmacists
keywords: pharmacist, influence, purchase decisions, marketing strategies, target, market analysis
rationale: The abstract discusses the role of pharmacists in influencing pharmaceutical purchase decisions in Egypt, which involves a level of market analysis and targeting specific demographics (e.g., social classes). The mention of survey data and cluster analysis aligns with the use of marketing analytics to understand competitive advantages and customer behavior. This indicates a focus on strategic analysis rather than mechanical processes or emotional understanding.
resumo: O objetivo deste artigo é explorar o papel do farmacêutico como prescritor, influenciador, trocador e dispensador de medicamentos em um país em desenvolvimento, o Egito. Os autores realizaram uma pesquisa com farmacêuticos no Cairo, que estimaram as porcentagens de pacientes que chegaram com receita, apenas com uma caixa ou recomendação de medicamento e apenas com sintomas, além de informar se trocaram o paciente para outro medicamento. As farmácias foram classificadas de acordo com a classe social dos bairros. A análise de cluster foi utilizada para classificar os farmacêuticos como "Influenciadores" e "Não influenciadores". Os resultados mostraram que os farmacêuticos influenciam 39% de todas as decisões de compra de medicamentos, com maior influência em bairros de classe social mais baixa. Aproximadamente um em cada quatro farmacêuticos foi classificado como Influenciador. Em países em desenvolvimento, o farmacêutico desempenha um papel fundamental na escolha dos medicamentos que os pacientes compram. Atividades de marketing direcionadas aos farmacêuticos podem representar uma oportunidade importante para maximizar o retorno sobre o investimento em marketing das empresas farmacêuticas. Este estudo é único ao examinar o papel do farmacêutico nesses mercados, contribuindo para a compreensão dos desafios enfrentados pela indústria e suas implicações para as estratégias de marketing farmacêutico.

Title: GloStra - A hybrid system for developing global strategy and associated Internet strategy
Authors: Li S.; Davies B.J.
Abstract: An intelligent hybrid system, called GloStra (developed by the author), for developing global marketing strategy and associated Internet marketing strategy is reported in this paper. The hybrid system is built to integrate the strengths of expert systems, fuzzy logic, artificial neural networks and decision support technology; and to link the development of global marketing strategy with the formulation of associated Internet marketing strategy. In the paper, the system architecture, the functional modules of the hybrid system and other associated technical issues are addressed. The directions for further research in this field are also highlighted.
Keywords: Expert systems; Global marketing; Hybrid systems; Information systems; Marketing planning; Marketing strategy
keywords: global marketing strategy, Internet marketing strategy, expert systems, fuzzy logic, artificial neural networks, decision support technology
rationale: The abstract discusses the development of an intelligent hybrid system, GloStra, which integrates various AI technologies to formulate global marketing strategies and associated Internet marketing strategies. This aligns with the 'Thinking AI' category, particularly in the context of market analysis and strategic formulation, as it aims to identify and integrate strengths for competitive marketing advantage.
resumo: Um sistema híbrido inteligente, chamado GloStra (desenvolvido pelo autor), para desenvolver estratégias de marketing global e estratégias de marketing na Internet associadas é apresentado neste artigo. O sistema híbrido foi construído para integrar as forças de sistemas especialistas, lógica fuzzy, redes neurais artificiais e tecnologia de suporte à decisão; e para vincular o desenvolvimento da estratégia de marketing global com a formulação da estratégia de marketing na Internet associada. No artigo, a arquitetura do sistema, os módulos funcionais do sistema híbrido e outras questões técnicas associadas são abordados. As direções para pesquisas futuras neste campo também são destacadas.

Title: Big-data AI analytics in value-chain innovation and international marketing strategy: insights from SMEs in cultural and creative industries
Authors: Zong, ZP; Anwar, MA; Khan, S; Asmi, F; Hussain, N
Abstract: Purpose Despite great consensus on the positive impact of big-data-driven artificial intelligence (AI) analytics (BDAI) on a firm's performance, it still appears to be a black box mechanism through which small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) strengthen their dynamic competencies to innovate and expand their global footprint. To fill this theoretical and empirical gap we examine the relationship between BDAI affordances, digital marketing capabilities (DMCs), value-chain innovation and international market goals.Design/methodology/approach The study incorporates the dynamic capability view an extension of the resource-based view and the knowledge-based view to empirically examine the primary data collected from marketing managers and executives of SMEs in cultural and creative industries utilizing Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) analysis.Findings The study highlights the significant role of BDAI affordances such as intelligent process recommendations, customer intelligence and market intelligence on DMCs, where DMCs significantly affect value-chain innovation and international market strategy both directly and indirectly.Research limitations/implications The study minimizes the gap in identifying the BDAI affordances to drive innovation and international market strategy in the context of SMEs in cultural and creative industries. Marketing managers can incorporate these findings to enhance their digital capabilities for competitive advantages in international markets.Originality/value The study proposes a holistic framework of BDAI affordances for the strategic use of digital resources and knowledge to transform digital capabilities into new forms of value to expand in the international market. These insights are robust and grounded in findings provided by marketing practitioners.
Keywords: Big-data-based AI analytics; Digital affordances; Digital marketing capabilities; Value-chain innovation; International market strategy; Cultural and creative industries
keywords: big-data-driven artificial intelligence, digital marketing capabilities, value-chain innovation, international market strategy, customer intelligence, market intelligence
rationale: The abstract discusses the impact of big-data-driven AI analytics on the dynamic capabilities of SMEs, particularly in enhancing their digital marketing capabilities and driving innovation in the value chain. This aligns with the 'Thinking AI' category, as it focuses on strategic analysis, market analysis, and the use of insights to achieve international market goals. The elements of customer intelligence and market intelligence also suggest a focus on understanding the market environment and competitive advantages.
resumo: O estudo investiga como as affordances da inteligência artificial impulsionada por big data (BDAI) influenciam as competências de marketing digital (DMCs), a inovação na cadeia de valor e os objetivos de mercado internacional em pequenas e médias empresas (PMEs) nos setores cultural e criativo. Utilizando a modelagem de equações estruturais, os resultados mostram que as affordances da BDAI, como recomendações de processos inteligentes e inteligência de mercado, têm um papel significativo nas DMCs, que, por sua vez, impactam diretamente e indiretamente a inovação na cadeia de valor e a estratégia de mercado internacional. O estudo sugere um framework holístico para o uso estratégico de recursos digitais e conhecimento, permitindo que as PMEs transformem suas capacidades digitais em novas formas de valor para expansão no mercado internacional.

Title: Business interest associations in the USA and Europe: evaluation of digital marketing techniques applied on their websites and social networks
Authors: Ponzoa J.M.; Gómez A.; Arilla R.
Abstract: Purpose: This study aims to develop a proprietary indicator to measure the digital presence of the institutions: the digital presence index. Design/methodology/approach: This research delves into how nonprofit institutions, specifically business interest associations (BIAs), have developed their internet presence by applying essential digital marketing techniques. To this end, and using big data mining tools, this study analyzes the tracking by internet users of 102 BIAs, with their respective websites in 36 countries in Europe and the USA. In addition, the presence and activity of the institutions included in this study on social networks are considered. Findings: This research serves as a basis for discussing the current gap between social reality and the digitalization of institutions. In this sense, conclusions are drawn on the importance of managerial profiles in decision-making on digitization and the necessary knowledge that, together with Web and social network managers, they must have to articulate the means and techniques that promote the internet presence of the organizations they manage. Originality/value: Conclusions are drawn according to the geographical scope of the BIAs, and an argument is made about the difficulties of connection and loss of prominence of this type of institutions among their different target audiences, especially among the youngest and most digitized. © 2022, Emerald Publishing Limited.
Keywords: Business interest associations; Digital marketing; Digital presence index; Social networks
keywords: digital presence, digital marketing, internet presence, social networks, managerial profiles, decision-making, target audiences
rationale: The study focuses on analyzing the digital presence and marketing strategies of nonprofit institutions, specifically BIAs, which aligns with market analysis and targeting. It uses big data mining tools to evaluate online user engagement and the effectiveness of digital marketing techniques, indicating a strategic understanding of market dynamics. The emphasis on decision-making by managerial profiles further supports its classification under Thinking AI.
resumo: Este estudo tem como objetivo desenvolver um indicador proprietário para medir a presença digital das instituições, denominado índice de presença digital. A pesquisa investiga como as instituições sem fins lucrativos, especificamente associações de interesse empresarial (AIEs), têm aprimorado sua presença na internet por meio da aplicação de técnicas essenciais de marketing digital. Utilizando ferramentas de mineração de big data, o estudo analisa o acompanhamento de 102 AIEs por usuários da internet, com seus respectivos sites em 36 países da Europa e dos EUA, além de considerar a presença e atividade dessas instituições nas redes sociais. Os resultados discutem a lacuna atual entre a realidade social e a digitalização das instituições, ressaltando a importância dos perfis gerenciais na tomada de decisões sobre a digitalização e o conhecimento necessário que, junto aos gerentes de web e redes sociais, devem ter para articular os meios e técnicas que promovam a presença na internet das organizações que gerenciam. As conclusões são baseadas no escopo geográfico das AIEs, abordando as dificuldades de conexão e a perda de destaque desse tipo de instituição entre seus diferentes públicos-alvo, especialmente entre os mais jovens e digitalizados.

Title: Recommender systems impact on Platform’s content and outcomes: the role of providers and algorithm designs
Authors: Mohammadi Darani M.; Aghaie S.
Abstract: Purpose: The study aims to investigate how recommender systems shape providers’ dynamics and content offerings on platforms, and to provide insights into algorithm designs for achieving better outcomes in platform design. Design/methodology/approach: This study employs a multi-agent simulation framework coupled with reinforcement learning models to examine the influence of different recommender system designs on providers’ perception of demand and platform content. Findings: The study reveals that recommender systems have the potential to introduce biases in providers’ understanding of user preferences, thereby impacting the variety of offerings on platforms. Moreover, it identifies algorithm design as a critical factor, with item-based collaborative filters showcasing superior performance in contexts where customers exhibit selectivity. Conversely, user-based models prove more effective in scenarios where recommendations significantly sway user decisions, ultimately boosting sales. Practical implications: In practical terms, these insights can guide platform developers in making informed decisions regarding the selection and implementation of recommender system algorithms. By tailoring algorithm choices to specific contexts, platforms can enhance user welfare, ultimately leading to improved platform performance and profitability. Originality/value: The findings underscore the importance of integrating provider dynamics and algorithmic biases into the design of recommender systems and platforms. This highlights avenues for future research to explore and refine our understanding of these dynamics. © 2024, Emerald Publishing Limited.
Keywords: Digital marketing; Platform design; Recommender systems; Sales diversity
keywords: recommender systems, algorithm design, provider dynamics, user preferences, market performance, personalization
rationale: The abstract discusses the impact of recommender systems on providers' understanding of demand and platform content, which aligns with market analysis and targeting strategies. The findings highlight how different algorithm designs can influence user decision-making, revealing a focus on strategic analysis and personalization based on customer preferences. This indicates a clear connection to the Thinking AI category.
resumo: O estudo investiga como os sistemas de recomendação moldam a dinâmica dos provedores e as ofertas de conteúdo nas plataformas, além de fornecer insights sobre o design de algoritmos para alcançar melhores resultados no design de plataformas. Utilizando uma estrutura de simulação multiagente combinada com modelos de aprendizado por reforço, a pesquisa examina a influência de diferentes designs de sistemas de recomendação na percepção de demanda dos provedores e no conteúdo da plataforma. Os resultados revelam que os sistemas de recomendação podem introduzir vieses na compreensão das preferências dos usuários pelos provedores, impactando a variedade de ofertas nas plataformas. O design do algoritmo é identificado como um fator crítico, com filtros colaborativos baseados em itens apresentando desempenho superior em contextos onde os clientes são seletivos. Em contrapartida, modelos baseados em usuários se mostram mais eficazes em cenários onde as recomendações influenciam significativamente as decisões dos usuários, aumentando as vendas. Essas descobertas podem orientar os desenvolvedores de plataformas na escolha e implementação de algoritmos de sistemas de recomendação, melhorando o bem-estar dos usuários e, consequentemente, o desempenho e a lucratividade das plataformas. Os resultados ressaltam a importância de integrar a dinâmica dos provedores e os vieses algorítmicos no design de sistemas de recomendação e plataformas, abrindo caminhos para futuras pesquisas sobre essas dinâmicas.

Title: Out of the fog: fog computing-enabled AI to support smart marketing management
Authors: Hornik J.; Ofir C.; Rachamim M.
Abstract: Marketing and consumer research use a variety of data and electronic measurement devices for research, theory-building, and applied decision-making. Managing data deluge produced by ‘smart devices’ and internet of things (IoT) actuators and sensors is one of the challenges faced by managers when using IoT systems. With the advent of the cloud-based IoT and artificial intelligence, which are advancing a ‘smart world’ and introducing automation in many application areas, such as ‘smart marketing,’ a need has arisen for various modifications to support the IoT devices that are at the center of the automation world, including recent language models like, ChatGPT and Bart, and technologies like nanotechnology. The article introduces the marketing community to a recent computing development: IoT-driven fog computing (FC)—an emerging concept that decentralizes operations, management, and data into the network utilizing a distributed and federated computing paradigm. Although numerous research studies have been published on ‘smart’ applications, none hitherto have been conducted on fog-based smart marketing. FC is considered a novel computational system, which can mitigate latency and improve bandwidth utilization for autonomous marketing applications requiring real-time processing of ‘big data’ typical of smart marketing ecosystems. © The Author(s) 2024.
Keywords: Artificial intelligence (AI); Digital marketing; Edge computing; Fog computing; Marketing internet of things (MIoT); O; Smart marketing; Software defined networks (SDN)
keywords: data deluge, IoT systems, automation, fog computing, real-time processing, big data
rationale: The abstract discusses the use of IoT devices and fog computing in marketing contexts, primarily focusing on managing data collection and processing in 'smart marketing' ecosystems. It emphasizes the automation of data handling and processing, which aligns with the definitions provided for Mechanical AI, particularly in data collection and standardization processes. While the abstract mentions new technologies and improvements in operational efficiency, it does not delve into emotional understanding or market analysis, which would relate it to the other categories.
resumo: O marketing e a pesquisa do consumidor utilizam uma variedade de dados e dispositivos de medição eletrônica para pesquisa, construção de teorias e tomada de decisões aplicadas. Gerenciar o grande volume de dados produzidos por 'dispositivos inteligentes' e sensores da internet das coisas (IoT) é um dos desafios enfrentados pelos gerentes ao usar sistemas IoT. Com o advento da IoT baseada em nuvem e da inteligência artificial, que estão promovendo um 'mundo inteligente' e introduzindo automação em várias áreas de aplicação, como o 'marketing inteligente', surgiu a necessidade de várias modificações para apoiar os dispositivos IoT que estão no centro do mundo da automação, incluindo modelos de linguagem recentes como ChatGPT e Bart, e tecnologias como a nanotecnologia. O artigo apresenta à comunidade de marketing um recente desenvolvimento computacional: a computação em névoa (FC) impulsionada pela IoT — um conceito emergente que descentraliza operações, gerenciamento e dados na rede, utilizando um paradigma de computação distribuída e federada. Embora numerosos estudos de pesquisa tenham sido publicados sobre aplicações 'inteligentes', nenhum até agora foi realizado sobre marketing inteligente baseado em névoa. A FC é considerada um sistema computacional inovador, que pode mitigar a latência e melhorar a utilização da largura de banda para aplicações de marketing autônomas que exigem processamento em tempo real de 'big data', típico dos ecossistemas de marketing inteligente.

Title: The interplay of artificial intelligence, machine learning, and data analytics in digital marketing and promotions: a review and research agenda
Authors: Basu R.; Aktar M.N.; Kumar S.
Abstract: In contemporary data-driven business environments, the adoption of artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and data analytics has enabled the practice of digital marketing and promotions with incomparable efficiency. To provide insights into the current trends and future directions of research in this overlapping knowledge cluster, the present study examines 94 published journal articles to date obtained from the Scopus database. Utilizing the systematic performance analysis and review method (SPAR-4-SLR), the paper uses Excel and VOSviewer to present a bibliometric review. Following a thorough disciplinary analysis of the articles, the paper identifies five main research clusters representing the domain (i) AI and Digital Marketing (ii) Branding Automation and Engagement (iii) Optimizing E-Commerce and Social Media Marketing (iv) AI-Powered Personalized Marketing (v) Emerging Tools in Digital Marketing. In this paper, we draw on some of the key theories relevant to the field and develop an Antecedent-Decision-Outcome framework that examines the factors affecting the use of digital technologies and the benefits derived from them. Pivotal research questions are also articulated in this study to guide future inquiries in this evolving area of study. © The Author(s), under exclusive licence to Springer Nature Limited 2024.
Keywords: Artificial intelligence; Bibliometric review; Digital marketing; Digital promotions; Machine learning
keywords: artificial intelligence, digital marketing, machine learning, personalized marketing, e-commerce, branding automation, data analytics
rationale: The abstract discusses the application of AI and data analytics in enhancing digital marketing efficiency, focusing on market analysis, targeting, and personalization. The identified research clusters align with the strategic analysis aspects of Thinking AI, particularly in optimizing marketing efforts and personalizing experiences based on customer data. There is no emphasis on emotional understanding or relational aspects that would indicate Feeling AI, nor does it focus solely on automated processes that would classify it as Mechanical AI.
resumo: Nos ambientes de negócios contemporâneos orientados por dados, a adoção de inteligência artificial (IA), aprendizado de máquina (ML) e análise de dados possibilitou a prática de marketing digital e promoções com eficiência incomparável. Este estudo examina 94 artigos de periódicos publicados até o momento, obtidos da base de dados Scopus, para fornecer insights sobre as tendências atuais e direções futuras da pesquisa nesse cluster de conhecimento. Utilizando o método de análise de desempenho sistemática e revisão (SPAR-4-SLR), o artigo apresenta uma revisão bibliométrica por meio do Excel e VOSviewer. Após uma análise disciplinar minuciosa dos artigos, o estudo identifica cinco principais clusters de pesquisa representando o domínio: (i) IA e Marketing Digital, (ii) Automação de Branding e Engajamento, (iii) Otimização de E-Commerce e Marketing em Mídias Sociais, (iv) Marketing Personalizado Potencializado por IA, (v) Ferramentas Emergentes em Marketing Digital. O artigo também aborda algumas das principais teorias relevantes para o campo e desenvolve um modelo de Antecedente-Decisão-Resultado que examina os fatores que afetam o uso de tecnologias digitais e os benefícios derivados delas. Questões de pesquisa fundamentais são articuladas para orientar investigações futuras nesta área em evolução.

Title: The role of absorptive capacity in the use of digital marketing analytics for effective marketing decisions
Authors: Proença, M; Martins, TS
Abstract: According to the literature, companies that use consumer data from digital marketing can have better results than those that do not. However, investments in analytics have gradually declined and most research does not place the use of data in strategic processes. Thus, this paper proposes a model to evaluate the incorporation of external knowledge generated by data, with the organization's internal knowledge, through the insertion of the absorptive capacity as a mediator between the use of digital marketing data and the effectiveness of marketing decision-making. To this end, a survey of 144 Brazilian retail companies was conducted and it was found that there is mediation, but it is partial. The findings suggest some insights into actions that can be taken to improve the use of data by the organization, such as the importance of disseminating marketing data, so that it can be used strategically by decision-makers.

The incorporation of absorptive capacity as a mediator suggests a sophisticated analysis of data rather than just mechanical collection or emotional understanding, which aligns it closely with the Thinking AI category.
resumo: De acordo com a literatura, empresas que utilizam dados de consumidores do marketing digital podem obter resultados melhores do que aquelas que não o fazem. Assim, este artigo propõe um modelo para avaliar a incorporação do conhecimento externo gerado por dados, juntamente com o conhecimento interno da organização, através da inserção da capacidade absorvente como mediadora entre o uso de dados de marketing digital e a eficácia da tomada de decisões de marketing. Para isso, foi realizada uma pesquisa com 144 empresas de varejo brasileiras e constatou-se que há mediação, mas ela é parcial. Os achados sugerem algumas ideias sobre ações que podem ser tomadas para melhorar o uso de dados pela organização, como a importância de disseminar dados de marketing, para que possam ser utilizados estrategicamente pelos tomadores de decisão.

Title: Developing big data enabled Marketing 4.0 framework
Authors: Mukhopadhyay S.; Singh R.K.; Jain T.
Abstract: Due to the industrial revolution and, thereby with, the emergence of Industry 4.0, there has been an impact on the marketing of business firms, enabling them to digitally transform and adopt Marketing 4.0 practices supported by smart technologies. One of these is Big Data Analytics (BDA), which enables a firm to improve its marketing practices. The main objective of this study is to evaluate how integrating big data technology improves the marketing strategies of Indian FMCG companies operating in a dynamic and highly competitive market distinguished by its size and diversity, constantly changing consumer behaviour, and Marketing 4.0 trends. This study adopts a systematic approach to coding an interview with seasoned Indian FMCG professionals to explain the capabilities of Big Data in molding marketing practices. A framework is constructed based on the same. The theoretical and practical implications are discussed to visualize its applicability in business. Further, the Resource-based View (RBV) theory is discussed for describing the insights into the role and adoption of Big Data by Indian FMCG firms for enhancing performance and achieving competitiveness, along with demonstrating its benefits for decision-making, customer loyalty and internal capability assessment. © 2024 The Author(s)

keywords: Big Data Analytics, marketing strategies, competitive market, consumer behaviour, decision-making, customer loyalty
